strings.str_hsim_us_tut_05_steps_liftuphigh_1: Slowly increase collective to lift up high into the air. Apply pedal pressure to maintain your heading.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_05_steps_liftup_2: You left the take off area!
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_05_steps_liftup_1: Slowly increase the collective to lift up into the air. Apply pedal pressure to maintain your heading.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_05_steps_hovering_1:
Hovering is the act of keeping the helicopter steady over a reference point, at a constant altitude and fixed heading. This is a difficult maneuver, requiring constant concentration and coordination.

Try to prevent over-controlling by only making small input corrections when you start detecting changes in attitude or altitude. When you detect forward movement, use aft cyclic to correct. Before coming to a halt remove the correction, so as not to start moving backwards.

Your main visual focus should be a little distance away from the helicopter. Be aware of the point, but do not focus all your attention there. If you find yourself struggling with hovering, try using auto-hover.

strings.str_hsim_us_tut_04_steps_turns_1:
To enter a turn from straight flight, apply lateral cyclic (tilting the cyclic control left or right). Do not use the pedals to assist the turn; use them only to counteract torque. After reaching the desired bank angle, return the cyclic to a neutral position. Increase the collective to maintain your altitude while doing this.

Rolling out of a turn is the opposite procedure, but make sure to start it before reaching the desired heading, because the helicopter will continue to turn for a while. Applying incorrect amounts of pedal pressure may cause your aircraft to slip towards the centre of the turn (the turn is too fast), or away from it (turn is too slow).

strings.str_hsim_us_tut_04_steps_trimming_1:
Depending on your difficulty options, you have access two various stability aids.

%1 Manual trim: this allows changing the neutral position of your flight controls to a specific position (set when activated). If you need to constantly apply some cyclic in a certain direction while cruising, you can set manual trim and rest the cyclic. Removing manual trim returns all controls to their default centre neutral positions.
%2 Auto-trim: some difficulty levels allow auto-trim, which handles a lot of the antitorque corrections for you.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_04_steps_straightflight_:
In straight flight a constant altitude and heading are maintained. You have control over airspeed by changing the attitude (or orientation) (cyclic pitch) of the helicopter. By moving the nose down (i.e. forward cyclic) you will generate forward thrust, but this requires more lift to maintain altitude (i.e. raised collective). Decreasing airspeed is done by applying aft cyclic and lowering collective. Make sure not to exceed the maximum airspeed (the 'never exceed speed'), as it may cause structural damage or rotor stall.

Altitude is primarily controlled by the collective: raising it generates more lift, and lowering it reduces lift. Changing the collective position often results in a slight change of rotor RPMs, which in turn affects the torque. Counteract this effect by adjusting your pedal pressure (anti-torque rotor).

strings.str_hsim_us_tut_04_steps_descent_1:
In a normal descent the objective is to maintain a controlled rate of descent. Lower the collective and counteract torque using the pedals. Lower the nose using forward cyclic for a good descending attitude.

Level off using backward cyclic, raised collective and pedals for anti-torque control.

Use aft cyclic to reach the desired climb attitude, while using collective to gain enough climb power. Because of the increased torque you will need to compensate more using your pedals. Be aware that with greater weight, more lift is required to ascend.

A short while before reaching the target altitude, start leveling off using forward cyclic. Maintain climb power until you reach cruising airspeed.

strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_wait4cooldown_1: Wait 15 seconds to allow a period of cool down.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_wait4apu100_1: Wait for the APU to reach 100%.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_throttlefull_1: Bring engine up to full throttle.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_throttle_2:
The 'throttle' controls the introduction of fuel to the 'main engine'.

Controlled in three states - 'off', 'idle', and 'full' - when the throttle is set to full the governor takes over and stabilizes the engine RPM.

Throttle up / down
%7 (engine #1): %1 / %2
%7 (engine #2): %3 / %4
%7 (engine #3): %5 / %6
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_throttle_1:
The 'throttle' controls the introduction of fuel to the 'main engine'.

Controlled in three states - 'off', 'idle', and 'full' - more fuel results in higher RPM and, therefore, greater potential lift.

%7 Throttle up / down (engine #1): %1 / %2
%7 Throttle up / down (engine #2): %3 / %4
%7 Throttle up / down (engine #3): %5 / %6
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_starteron_1: Hold the starter to turn on the engine.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_starter_1:
The 'starter' uses electrical power to begin raising rotor-blade 'Revolutions Per Minute' (RPM).

It is used before the introduction of fuel. It can also prevent damage being caused to the engine by a 'Hot Start' as the spinning of engine cools it down.

A 'Hot Start' is a result of incorrectly starting an engine, often, where fuel is introduced too soon or two quickly to the engine, or engine is not cool enough (less then 150 deg).

%4 Starter toggle (engine #1): %1
%4 Starter toggle (engine #2): %2
%4 Starter toggle (engine #3): %3
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_rotorbreak_1:
The 'rotor brake' arrests the rotational movement of the main rotor.

The 'rotor brake' component is interconnected with the main rotor drive shaft, where the brake disc defines a plane perpendicular to the axis of the main transmission.

%2 Rotor brake toggle: %1
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_engine_1:
The main engine drives the rotational movement of the rotor-blades.

Most small helicopters, such as our training variant, use only one engine, which produces power for both the main and tail rotor systems.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_electricityon_1: Switch the electrical systems on, and keep an eye on the battery charge.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_electricalsyste:
Our electrical system requires powering on to use. The battery enables the use of electrical components, such as lights or communication devices, without the engine running.

However, it is chiefly used for starting the engine, which then operates as a generator. Unless connected to a 'Ground Power Unit', the system has a limited amount of charge to initiate start up.

The battery also acts as a backup system, providing emergency electrical power in the event of a generator failure.

%2 Batteries toggle: %1
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_steps_apu_1:
The 'Auxiliary Power Unit' is a small, extra engine, which is used to start the 'main engine'.

The 'APU' is switched off once fuel has been introduced into the 'main engine' and the 'starter' has been released.

%2 APU toggle: %1
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_stages_startupprocedu: Follow the instructor guidance to startup the helicopter.
Try to complete the manual startup procedure of the light helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_stages_shutdownproced: Follow the instructor's guidance to shutdown the helicopter.
Learn the manual shutdown procedure of the light helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_stages_corecomponents: Explanation of the core components involved in the startup and shutdown procedures.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_sum:
Getting a helicopter up and running, and shutting it back down again.
- Maddox

strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_im_2: T:haha, ah, Maddox, I'm sure you'll manage to ring up your Air Force buddies and get me shot down!
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_im_1: I:Now you know how to fire up my birds, make sure you don't sneak in and take them from me...
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_03_desc:
Pilot Training Invoice Summary

The Instructor will teach a common start-up and shutdown procedure.

The Trainee should attempt to memorize the procedures and then perform them on his own.
strings.str_hsim_wait4warmup_ins_1: This will allow our components to warm up.
strings.str_hsim_wait4warmup_ins_2: This warm-up is not necessary for the engine itself, but it will prevent stress and wear on other moving components.
strings.str_hsim_wait4enginedrop65_ins_0: Wait until the engine levels out at around 65 percent.
strings.str_hsim_wait4enginedrop65_ins_1: You should be able to hear the engine respond and bottom out.
strings.str_hsim_wait4enginedrop65_ins_2: We still need to monitor our gauges.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine65_ins_0: Wait for the engine to reach approximately 65 percent.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine65_ins_1: you can check the gauge on the panel to verify this.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine65_ins_2: While we're idling, it won't exceed this speed.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine12_ins_0: Verify that the engine has reached at least 12 percent.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine12_ins_1: We can also check that the Turbine Outlet Temperature, or 'TOT', is below 150 degrees.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine12_ins_2: Remember, it's vital that you do not release the starter at this stage.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine100_ins_0: Wait until the engine reaches its max rpm.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine100_ins_1: Once we're there, we'll have enough potential power to generate lift.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine100_ins_2: But to do that, we'll wait until the next lesson.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine0_ins_0: Wait until the blades are at zero rpm.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine0_ins_1: Great work so far, once we're at zero, we're done here.
strings.str_hsim_wait4engine0_ins_2: I hope you've been making notes, as next up I'll ask you to try things on your own!
strings.str_hsim_wait4cooldown_ins_0: Wait 15 seconds to allow a period of cool down.
strings.str_hsim_wait4cooldown_ins_1: Really, this step is just good practise.
strings.str_hsim_wait4cooldown_ins_2: Doing it helps to preserve the life-span of the components.
strings.str_hsim_wait4apu100_ins_0: Wait for the APU to reach 100 percent.
strings.str_hsim_wait4apu100_ins_1: Check the display panel to see the charge increasing.
strings.str_hsim_wait4apu100_ins_2: Meanwhile, we might double check to ensure the blades are clear of obstructions.
strings.str_hsim_throttleoff_ins_1: Here, we're ready to drop our RPMs further.
strings.str_hsim_throttleoff_ins_2: Check the gauges to track the slowdown.
strings.str_hsim_throttleidlestart_ins_0: Ok, now roll the throttle to 'flat idle'.
strings.str_hsim_throttleidlestart_ins_2: This will rapidly increase engine RPMs and get it properly started.
strings.str_hsim_throttleidleshut_ins_1: Firstly, we need to bring down the RPMs.
strings.str_hsim_throttleidleshut_ins_2: Be aware of strong cross-winds, which can still be dangerous during our shut-down.
strings.str_hsim_throttlefull_ins_0: Bring the engine up to full throttle.
strings.str_hsim_throttlefull_ins_1: This will rapidly increase the rotors' rpm.
strings.str_hsim_throttlefull_ins_2: Consult the centre panel to monitor the rpm.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_non_narrative_ins_0: This lesson will cover the basics of starting up and shutting down the helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_non_narrative_ins_1: First, with guidance, we'll try a start up and shut down.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_non_narrative_ins_2: Then, we'll repeat the process with no assistance.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_end_ins_1: You even made it through without totalling my turbines - I can only be impressed!
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_end_ins_2: Well, I wouldn't be so sure, I remember a certain other Larkin that was only seconds away from a hot start...
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_end_ins_3: Hah! No, not old Harry. You didn't know? I taught your brother some things too!
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_end_pla_0: Ah, I'm sure it was down to the good instruction, Maddox.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_end_ins_4: Oh, hell, you can't let him know I told you, though, he swore me to secrecy!
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_end_ins_5: Ok, see you next time, Tom!
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_end_pla_2: Ah, well, that is useful information for a younger brother to have, Maddox, but your secret's safe with me.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_ins_0: Welcome again, Tom. Today, we're finally gonna get to grips with the chopper.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_ins_1: Well, we'll start at the most logical place: the start-up sequence.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_ins_2: Now, starting a turbine helicopter can be very simple; however, it can also be a very fast and very expensive mess up if you're not careful.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_pla_0: Great, so, where do we begin, Maddox?
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_ins_3: I've know a number of - often pretty experienced - pilots lose everything from one botched start up.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_narrative_ins_4: Heh, and no, your pop isn't included in that number, Tom.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_intro_ins_0: The start-up sequence varies with every helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_intro_ins_1: You might want to make notes or find some method of remembering these basic procedures.
strings.str_hsim_start_up_intro_ins_2: In general, we should proceed as follows.
strings.str_hsim_starteron_ins_0: Hold the starter to turn on the engine.
strings.str_hsim_starteron_ins_1: This will use the electrical power unit to start raising the engine RPMs.
strings.str_hsim_starteron_ins_2: We need to do this to prevent what's known as a 'hot start'.
strings.str_hsim_shut_down_intro_ins_0: As you might guess, shutting down a helicopter isn't a simple matter of taking the key out of the ignition.
strings.str_hsim_shut_down_intro_ins_1: We'll follow the shut-down procedure carefully, both for safety and for the long-term integrity of the bird.
strings.str_hsim_releasestarter_ins_1: Note that releasing the starter prematurely can cause a 'hot start'.
strings.str_hsim_releasestarter_ins_2: A hot start may critically damage your engine.
strings.str_hsim_explanation_intro_ins_0: I've compiled some notes, which explain the sequences.
strings.str_hsim_explanation_intro_ins_1: This should give you the idea for each stage.
strings.str_hsim_electricityon_ins_0: Switch the batteries on, and keep an eye on the charge.
strings.str_hsim_electricityon_ins_1: To use our electrical systems, we need to power them up.
strings.str_hsim_electricityon_ins_2: Unless we're connected to a GPU - the Ground Power Unit - we only have limited number of start-up attempts before running out.
strings.str_hsim_electricityoff_ins_1: We needn't waste our limited battery charge.
strings.str_hsim_blind_start_intro_ins_0: Fine work so far, but here comes the test.
strings.str_hsim_blind_start_intro_ins_1: Carefully follow the start up procedure, being sure not to miss any of the steps.
strings.str_hsim_blind_start_intro_ins_2: If you've made any notes, you can refer to them, but you'll get little help from me!
strings.str_hsim_blind_shut_intro_ins_0: Fantastic stuff. Now for the last step.
strings.str_hsim_blind_shut_intro_ins_1: Recall the shut-down sequence, and follow each step in order.
strings.str_hsim_blind_shut_intro_ins_2: Again, I'll be monitoring, but, it's all down to you!
strings.str_hsim_apuon_ins_1: This is basically a small, extra engine used to start the main engine.
strings.str_hsim_apuon_ins_2: Many helicopters, aside from the lightest ones, require an 'Auxiliary Power Unit' - the 'APU' - to start their engines.
strings.str_hsim_apuoff_ins_1: The engine is generating enough power on its own now.
strings.str_hsim_apuoff_ins_2: Leaving it on will only drain electricity needlessly.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_whatishelicopte: Helicopters are aircraft whose lift is generated by one or more engine-driven rotor systems. Their main advantage over fixed-wing aircraft is the ability to vertically lift off, land, to hover, and to fly forward, aftwards and sideways. These characteristics allow helicopters to reach places that other vehicles cannot.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_weight_1:
Make sure the aircraft does not exceed the maximum gross weight, which can cause structural deformations and affects handling.

First off, there is the basic empty weight, which is the airframe itself. Then, there is the 'useful load', which contains the flight crew, fuel and payload. The payload is any passenger, cargo and baggage. The sum of basic empty weight and useful load is the gross weight.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_weather_1:
Always respect the weather.

Too many people are killed each year from poor pre-flight planning. Pilots encounter bad weather and end up crashing into the ground due to the loss of visual references. Wind can affect your ability to control the aircraft, especially in situations where you need to keep a stable hover.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_torqueandantito:
Torque is the rotational movement caused by the main rotor in powered flight.

Antitorque counteracts this and is used for heading control. It is controlled by the pilot's pedals and used to rotate in a hover, and compensate for torque changes. Failure of this system usually causes a spin.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_tailrotor_1: Check the security of all attaching bolts, pitch-links, nuts, cotter-pins, etcetera of the tail rotor and the condition of blade, freedom of movement.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_rotorsystems_1:
The main rotor system provides the helicopter horizontal and vertical lift, enabling it to move in all directions. The blades can move in three distinct ways: flap (up and down), feather (rotation around span-wise axis / pitch angle), and lead / lag (back and forth in the plane of rotation).

Types of main rotor system:

%1 Fully articulated: all blades can move independently
(flap, feather and lead / lag)
%2 Semi-rigid: only flap and feather
%3 Rigid: only feather
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_rotorbladecolli:
It can be very difficult to judge the distance between rotor blade tips and obstructions. Pay extra attention near hangars and other objects in the environment. In some types of helicopter, you can't see the tail rotor from the cabin, so allow for more than enough clearance.

A loss of main rotor results in critical failure. Losing a tail rotor usually means you'll enter a spin. This situation can be recovered from by executing an immediate emergency procedure (autorotation).
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_preflightchecks:
As the Pilot In Command (PIC) you are ultimately responsible for safety during operation. Conduct regular and thorough inspections of the helicopters (both interior and exterior). Don't like what you find? Consult with your mechanic.

%1 Ensure instruments, sensors and controls are not obstructed.
%2 Check for leaks in hydraulics, fuel and oil systems.
%3 See if there are any objects under the belly, or in compartments.
%4 Make sure you have enough fuel in your helicopter.
%5 Look to see moving parts are not too loose, by seeing if drawn torque stripes have been interrupted
%6 Investigate visual damage, such as dings, nicks, scratches and corrosion
%7 Refer to the specific rotorcraft's flight manual, pilot's operating handbook, or similar information from the operator or manufacturer.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_pitots_1: Check if the pitots need to be cleared.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_otherapplicatio:
Other uses of helicopters include, but are not limited to:

%1 Aerial photography
%2 Motion picture filming
%3 News gathering and reporting (ENG - Electronic News Gathering)
%4 Search and Rescue
%5 Tourism and recreation
%6 Transport
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_military_1:
A lot of different types of helicopters are used by military forces all around the globe. Some are dedicated to troop and materiel transport, whereas others are specialized attack helicopters with advanced weapons systems.

Other applications include anti-submarine warfare and of course Search and Rescue duties. Recent developments include unmanned helicopter platforms, used primarily for intelligence gathering.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_mainrotor_1: Check rotor for dents, de-lamination, and anything that looks questionable.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_lawenforcement_:
Many police departments and other law enforcement agencies use helicopters in a variety of roles. They provide air support when tracking suspects, and are equipped with specialized cameras and search lights.

Another application of helicopters is getting tactical police officers to a scene rapidly, by deploying them from ropes suspended from the cabin: fast-roping.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_landinggear_1: Inspect the condition and functionality of the skids.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_interactingwith:
In many situations you are able to interact with objects around you (e.g. parts of a helicopter). To see available actions around you, use freelook mode. This will show precise positions on objects where actions are available, such as on switches in a cockpit.

%3 Freelook: %1
%3 Freelook toggle: %2

There are two primary methods:

%4 Default actions: context-sensitive and highlighted by pointing the cursor at them
%5 Action menu: selected from a list when multiple actions are available
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_hovering_1:
This is achieved by ensuring that enough lift and thrust are generated to equal weight and drag. The helicopter maintains the same position over a fixed position, usually not too high. The main rotor lift can be changed to move up or down, and the tail rotor is used to rotate.

Ground Effect: you can be Out of Ground Effect (OGE) or In Ground Effect (IGE). IGE occurs when hovering near the ground and is caused by airflow through the rotor disc as it's reduced by hitting the surface. The aircraft has more lift at the same blade angle. The effect is strongest in no-wind conditions and over firm, smooth surfaces.

OGE occurs when hovering at least a full rotor blade length or more above the ground. The effect is a need for the pilot to increase the collective to maintain a steady hover. This reduces the amount of actual power the pilot has available and thus at certain higher altitudes OGE may not be possible.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_helicopterconst:
Basic helicopters consist of a single main rotor and tail rotor, both powered by a powerplant. Suspended under the main rotor is a hull with a cockpit and cabin, which itself sits upon on a landing gear system.

The helicopter can use skids, wheels or floats for landing, and these systems usually have dampers to absorb shocks. Various vertical and horizontal stabilizers provide directional stability during flight.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_fueltank_1: Take off the fuel-cap and visually check the level.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_flying_1:
Up in the air, never become complacent. Never get too relaxed, comfortable, or develop a 'it won't happen to me'-type attitude.

Everything you do as a pilot must be assessed for the level of risk involved with a certain task or mission. Whenever in flight, have a landing site chosen, just in case you have to perform an emergency landing.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_flight_1:
%1 Forward: achieved by moving some of the vertical thrust forward. This is done by pilots using the cyclic control in their cockpit. If lift exceeds weight, the helicopter climbs; if lift is less than weight, it descends. If thrust is more than drag, the helicopter accelerates; if thrust is less than drag, it slows down.

%1 Sideways: the cyclic is used to vector thrust forward, the same can be done by vectoring to either side and cause lateral movement.

%1 Rearward: moving the cyclic back causes the helicopter to start moving backwards.

%1 Turning: using the cyclic one can bank the helicopter left and right and initiate a turn in forward flight.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_finandstabilise: Check condition and security of the vertical fin and horizontal stabilisers; verify no play or movement, dings, dents, etcetera.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_exhaustobstruct: Check the exhaust for any obstructions.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_executingaction:
After selecting an action by scrolling, you can execute the selected action.

%2 Execute action: %1

Often, you will have one primary action available to you in the current context. This can make that action the default selection. You can recognize a default action has been selected by seeing its icon and / or tool tip displayed near your cursor.

When you execute the action, it will be the default one. Note that even when a default action is selected, more actions may be available to you when using the Action Menu.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_downwash_1:
The thrust of the main rotor can blow sand, dust, water and more at a high velocity and cause injury or damage. Shield your eyes from downwash, and be wary of nearby people and objects.

For the pilot, kicked up dust can cause a 'brown-out', meaning your visibility is severely hampered.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_boarding_1:
In most cases, passengers should only board or be allowed to depart when the rotors are not spinning. They should approach and leave in a crouching manner and do so from the side or the front, in view of the pilot.

Never approach or depart the helicopter towards the tail rotor.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_ascendinganddes:
In order to ascend, you need more lift and thrust. This is achieved by increasing the angle of attack of the main rotor blades. Pilots use their collective control to do this.

The pilot should slow their airspeed before increasing collective to get the most effective rate of climb. High rate of speed with high collective (power) will place undue stress on the aircraft, reducing component lifespan.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_antitorquesyste:
%1 Tail rotor: the most common solution, using a smaller vertical rotor system on the tail boom

%1 Airflow: a new system uses a fan inside the tail boom and thrusts it for quieter and safer operation

%1 Tandem: two or more horizontal rotors turning in opposite directions

%1 Coaxial: two rotors mounted above one another in the same axis

%1 Tilt-rotor: two or more rotors mounted on rotating shafts on the tips of fixed wings (helicopter / airplane hybrid)
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_airambulance_1:
MEDEVAC helicopters are employed when traditional ambulances cannot quickly get to the the scene of trauma, or cannot reach it at all. In other cases aerial transport is simply the safest and quickest way of transporting patients between medical facilities.

These aircraft are equipped with medical equipment to allow caring for patients mid-flight.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_aerodynamicforc:
Four forces act on a helicopter in forward flight:

%1 Lift: upward force created by airflow around the airfoils
(in helicopters the blades, in airplanes the wings)
%2 Weight: opposing lift and caused by gravity
%3 Thrust: propelling the helicopter through the air
%4 Drag: caused by movement of an object through air
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_aerialfirefight: Forest fires are often hard to fight from the ground, so helicopters are often used to identify the fires. They can then also be fitted with water tanks or externally slung buckets. After taking in water in a nearby body of water, the helicopters can drop it over the fires accurately and quickly.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_aerialcrane_1:
Helicopters can be used to carry external loads, connected by long cables, to and from areas that other means of transport have difficulty getting to.

Examples of such sling load operations are placing heavy transmission towers, carrying trees during logging and even transporting ground vehicles.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_steps_accessingaction:
The Action Menu is a list of all actions currently available to you. You can access the menu by scrolling to the next or previous action.

%3 Next action: %1
%3 Previous action: %2
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_stages_vehicleinspect: Walk around the helicopter and complete the standard pre-flight inspection.
Object interaction and pre-flight vehicle inspection practice.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_stages_safetywarnings: The basics of the safety warnings to survive operating around helicopters.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_stages_objectinteract: Explanation of the different ways of interacting with in-game objects.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_stages_helicoptersins: Description of the most common uses of helicopters.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_stages_helicopterbasi: Introduction to the helicopter's basics and terminology.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_stages_flyingprincipl: Introduction to the principles of flying helicopter aircraft.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_sum:
Get educated about helicopters generally.
- Maddox

strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_im_3: I:Yeah, you'd be surprised just how many people actually think there's no difference between helos and planes.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_im_2: T:Sure, Maddox - honestly - I had no idea about some of that, so it's good to know!

strings.str_hsim_us_tut_01_desc:
Pilot Training Invoice Summary

The instructor will introduce the theory of helicopters: principles of flight, their potential application, and apects of interaction with the chopper.

The trainee will then be taught how to perform an exterior pre-flight inspection, while learning about critical components.
strings.str_hsim_inspection_intro_ins_0: Our next step is the pre-flight inspection.
strings.str_hsim_inspection_intro_ins_1: It's an important process, verifing the integrity of crucial systems. In general, we're inspecting any visible damage to fuselage.
strings.str_hsim_inspection_intro_ins_2: If a part on the helicopter has dings, nicks, scratches, or corrosion, it probably shouldn't be there. Use your head.
strings.str_hsim_interaction_intro_ins_0: Now, we'll get comfortable with how to properly interact with the helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_terms_intro_ins_0: Ok, we'll start off with the very basics of helicopter flight.
strings.str_hsim_terms_intro_ins_1: I'll take you through some important terminology and principles.
strings.str_hsim_terms_intro_ins_2: This information should come in handy later on.
strings.str_hsim_safety_intro_ins_0: Now, we need to go through some important warning and safety advice.
strings.str_hsim_safety_intro_ins_1: We need to think about safety both on the ground and in the air.
strings.str_hsim_safety_intro_ins_2: First off, some basic tips for maintaining safety on the ground.
strings.str_hsim_introduction_non_narrative_ins_: Here, we've got the chance to introduce you to the helicopter, and explain some fundamentals of helicopter flight.
Hopefully, this will prove useful, as I may well refer to some of these features or concepts in future lessons!
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_end_ins_: Well, that's about it for now! You enjoy that, Tom?
Alright, enough with this 'sir' business, Tom! Please, 'Maddox' will do just fine.
Exactly. Alright now, just a final point: slow down!
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_end_pla_: Sure was a lot of information - but, all real useful stuff, sir.
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_end_ins_: Everything you do - pre-flight, pickup, takeoffs, turns, set-downs - everything should be done slow, smooth, and in control.
Too many people make fast inputs which can lead to exceeding an aircraft's limits - or possibly killing people.
Now, I think I mentioned something about a beer earlier, let's just see if I can remember how your pop got his nickname!
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_ins_0: Of course! Welcome, Tom - pleasure to meet you!
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_ins_1: Ah, you needn't tell me about Harry Larkin! I used to fly with 'Dirty Harry' back in the Air Cav.
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_pla_0: Hey, um, Mr Maddox, sir? Howard Maddox? Tom Larkin - I called earlier about flight instruction?
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_ins_2: God, Harry and I went way back, actually. A real fine man; his passing was a great loss to us all.
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_pla_1: Thank you, sir. I guess I'm here for something like a refresher course? My father actually taught me about choppers when I was younger...
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_ins_3: Not at all, Tom, there's actually a lot more to say about old Harry Larkin!
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_ins_4: But, c'mon - let's not waste any more time on sentimentalities now, that's what the bar's there for - after your first lesson, obviously!
strings.str_hsim_introduction_narrative_pla_2: That's kind of you to say, sir.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_tailrotor_ins_0: On the tail - often using torque stripes - we check the security of all attaching bolts, pitch-links, nuts, cotter-pins, etcetera.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_tailrotor_ins_1: Verify the condition of blade, freedom of movement - both flapping and pitch change - too.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_tailrotor_ins_2: The tail compensates for the drag of the transmission of the rotor system during auto-rotation and provides heading control.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_staticports_ins_0: The static ports must also be checked for obstructions.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_staticports_ins_1: These ports measure air pressure directly.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_staticports_ins_2: They are used as input for instruments such as the vertical speed indicator, or 'VSI'.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_pitots_ins_0: The Pitot tubes can be blocked by things like bugs. Check if they need to be cleared.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_pitots_ins_1: This tube, usually on the front of the helicopter, is used as input for various indicators.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_pitots_ins_2: The pitot provides information such as airspeed by measuring ram-air, which is the airflow impacting it.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_mainrotor_ins_0: Check both the top and bottom of the rotor-blade for dents, de-lamination, and anything that looks questionable.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_mainrotor_ins_1: The main rotor provides vertical and horizontal lift; it allows the helicopter to move forward, aft, left and right across the ground.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_mainrotor_ins_2: The rotor system can consist of a single main rotor - as in the case here - or dual rotors.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_landinggear_ins_0: Inspect the condition and functionality of the skids.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_landinggear_ins_1: Skids are the most often used landing gear, because they can be used to land on many types of terrain.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_landinggear_ins_2: They often have dampers so impact-shocks don't affect the main rotor.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_fueltank_ins_0: Inspect the fuel-cap and visually check the level.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_fueltank_ins_1: We need to inspect the fuel-level and check for leaks.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_fueltank_ins_2: Leaks in the system cause a drop of pressure, so these should be checked for too.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_finandstabilisers_ins_0: Check the condition and security of the vertical fin; verify no play or movement, dings, dents, etcetera.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_finandstabilisers_ins_1: The vertical and horizontal fins are designed to provide directional stability in forward flight.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_finandstabilisers_ins_2: The stabilisers decrease the pedal workload for the pilot and reduces the amount of power required by the tail rotor for directional control.
strings.str_hsim_inspect_exhaustobstructions_ins: Check the exhaust for any obstructions.
We're looking for anything that could obstruct the air flow.
That might even include bird's nests!
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_warninglights_1:
Between the analogue gauges you'll find various warning indicators. Generally, be wary when you start seeing yellow indicators, and prepare for emergencies in case of red lights.

%1 RPM: at least one engine is at idle RPMs (yellow) / no engines have enough RPMs (red)
%2 ENG: damage to engines
%3 TRQ: torque over 100% (yellow) / over-torque causing transmission damage (red)
%4 BATT: electricity level and battery damage
%5 FUEL: fuel level and fuel tank damage
%6 TEMP: engine temperatures
%7 MROT: damage to main rotor system
%8 ATRQ: damage to anti-torque system
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_verticalspeedin: Your Vertical Speed Indicator (VSI) shows the rate of climb or descent by measuring how fast the ambient air pressure changes. It is important to keep an eye on this instrument while hovering or landing, to ensure that you are not moving vertically at too great a rate, which may induce settling with power or vortex ring state.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_throttlecontrol: The twist grip (found on the end of the collective), can influence the engine RPM by controlling the flow of fuel. In many helicopters the throttle is not normally adjusted during flight, but used during starting and shutting down the engines.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_stabilityindica:
The stability indicator shows a cross representing your aircraft from above and a white dot showing its movement on the horizontal plane. Should auto-hover be enabled, a green dot is shown at the centre of the cross.

On the left of this indicator you see the current vertical speed. If the needle is in the middle, you are not moving vertically. The vertical speed is also shown on top of the indicator.

The right side is reserved for showing the actual collective pitch control position.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_speedindicator_:
This indicator shows the true speed over the terrain, as opposed to Indicated Air Speed.

Secondary needles are used to show minimum, maximum and target speeds in special cases, such as restricted flight segments.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_rpmstorqueandte:
Always be aware of your RPMs and torque indicators. Both have a yellow warning range and red range. Low RPMs means you simply don't generate enough lift for flight, whereas high torque can damage your transmission.

During engine start-up procedures, be aware of your temperatures, which can damage your engine if they rise too high. Let your helicopter cool down before attempting consecutive starts and be mindful of peaks while going to idle and full throttle. A hot start can ruin your helicopter as a machine, and your career as a pilot.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_pitotstaticinst:
The primary way of measuring a helicopter's speed is by using the flow of air through special sensors. Pitot tubes (usually at the front) measure air impacting them, while static ports read ambient air pressure. It is important to check these for blockage regularly, or faulty readings may occur.

Instruments using these sensors are the airspeed indicator, altimeter and vertical speed indicator.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_naviagationandw:
The right-most indicator is your compass and your flight heading towards the active waypoint or task position.

In its centre, an arrow indicates the current direction and strength of wind.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_horizonindicato: This artificial horizon shows your pitch and bank level compared to the horizon. Above it you'll find a reading of current G-forces.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_gyroscopicinstr:
Various gyroscopic instruments are usually installed in helicopters. Attitude indicators serve as artificial horizons and allow the pilot to see the orientation of his aircraft as compared to the horizon (its pitch and bank attitude), even in low-visibility conditions.

Heading indicators show the actual compass direction and allow navigation on a level more accurate than traditional magnetic compasses. The latter are still installed in many helicopters however.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_cyclicpitchcont: The cyclic pitch control is found in front of the pilot and it tilts the main rotor disk. It is the primary control for steering, for banking and pitching the nose and up down to control airspeed.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_collectivepitch:
On the left side of the pilot you will find the collective pitch control. It changes the pitch angle of all main rotor blades collectively and thus causes lift.

This is the primary way to control ascent and descent. Since altering collective pitch causes a change in the load on the engine, effectively changing the RPM, the engine automatically adjusts to correct and keep a constant RPM via the governor.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_batteries_1: Many advanced avionics and other electrical accessories require power, however in case of emergencies all helicopters can still be flown without it. Starting the engine uses power from the batteries, but once it's up and running they are charged by a generator. Limited operation of electrical systems such as radios and lights is possible without a running engine.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_antitorquepedal: The pedals at your feet control the tail rotor pitch and thus thrust of the tail rotor blades (or alternate antitorque system). While its primary use is to counteract torque, it's also employed to help turn left and right, particularly in a hover.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_analoggauges_1:
On lower difficulty levels you have access to an artificial layer of basic instruments to aid you in your flying. These gauges are available in both first-person and third-person views.

Based on your game options the gauges will show Metric or Imperial units.

%2 Toggle analogue gauges: %1
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_altitudeindicat:
This shows the true altitude over the terrain, so radar altitude without height restrictions.

Secondary needles can indicate minimum, maximum and target altitudes for specific gameplay segments.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_altimeter_1:
By detecting changes in ambient air pressure while passing through the atmosphere, the barometric altimeter is able to provide altitude above mean sea level or MSL.

Some helicopters come equipped with a radar altimeter, which measure altitude by bouncing radar waves off the surface below. They are only accurate up to approximately %1. This instrument determines actual above ground level or AGL.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_steps_airspeedindicat: By comparing the difference between the ram air pressure from the pitot tube with static air pressure, the airspeed is calculated. This results in the Indicated Air Speed (IAS) being displayed in the cockpit.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_stages_hud_1: Learn how to read the in-game Head-Up Display (HUD).
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_stages_flightinstrume: Explanation of the functionality of different pitot-static, gyroscopic and other flight instruments.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_stages_flightcontrols: Explanation of the helicopter's four flight controls.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_stages_cockpitpreview: Look around the cockpit and follow the instructor's directives.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_sum:
Your first look at the cockpit components and systems.
- Maddox
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_im_4: I:Ah, it might seem that way, but it's not a matter of turning the key, believe you me!
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_im_3: T:Haha, oh, it seems easy enough.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_im_2: I:...Only one little part remaining: starting up her engines!
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_im_1: I:We're almost ready to get these birds in the air.
strings.str_hsim_us_tut_02_desc:
Pilot Training Invoice Summary

The Instructor will provide an overview of the most important cockpit systems.

The Trainee will be asked to identify and point out various essential switches and buttons.
strings.str_hsim_throttle_ins_0: Find the throttle, it's on the same component as the starter.
strings.str_hsim_throttle_ins_1: It controls the introduction of fuel to the engine.
strings.str_hsim_throttle_ins_2: The throttle has three states: 'off', 'idle', and 'full'.
strings.str_hsim_starter_ins_0: Find the starter, located by your left hand.
strings.str_hsim_starter_ins_1: This uses an electrical power unit to start raising the engine RPMs.
strings.str_hsim_starter_ins_2: You must always use this before introducing fuel to the engine.
strings.str_hsim_rotorbrake_ins_0: Find the Rotor brake, located above you.
strings.str_hsim_rotorbrake_ins_1: This arrests the rotational movement of the main rotor.
strings.str_hsim_rotorbrake_ins_2: It's normally not a good idea to start up a chopper with the break engaged.
strings.str_hsim_lights_ins_0: Locate the switch for the lights, it too is on the central panel.
strings.str_hsim_lights_ins_1: These are used for landing in low light conditions.
strings.str_hsim_lights_ins_2: When active, you'll see a beam of light slightly in advance of the helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_hud_intro_ins_0: Let's move on and take a look at aspects of the in-cockpit Heads Up Display, or 'HUD'.
strings.str_hsim_hud_analogue_intro_ins_0: Finally, we'll look at the analogue HUD.
strings.str_hsim_gauges_intro_ins_0: I've compiled some notes about important gauges.
strings.str_hsim_gauges_intro_ins_1: It describes what they are, and what they mean.
strings.str_hsim_collisionlights_ins_0: Now, look for the collision lights control; it's near the previous switch.
strings.str_hsim_collisionlights_ins_1: These should be switched on in low visibility, and remain active during the flight.
strings.str_hsim_collisionlights_ins_2: They are small blinking lights, found on the tail, main rotor, bottom and each skid.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_non_narrative_ins_0: Now, we'll take a look inside the cockpit.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_non_narrative_ins_1: You'll be introduced to the gauges and cockpit components.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_non_narrative_ins_2: Then, we'll finish up by covering aspects of the heads up displays.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_end_ins_0: Alright, Tom, that's us for today.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_end_ins_1: Don't worry, well get more 'hands on' soon enough!
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_end_ins_2: Hah, yeah, that's more like old Harry...
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_end_ins_3: Alright, anyway, see you next time, Tom. Just gimmi a call.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_end_pla_0: Glad to hear it. I can't wait to get back up in the air.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_end_ins_4: Oh, and be sure to ask about 'Everon' some time - now that's a story your pop wouldn't have told ya'!
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_ins_0: Tom! Welcome back, so glad you could make it.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_ins_1: Good to hear! you've got your father's keen attitude, but we're not quite ready to get in to the air just yet.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_ins_2: Today, we'll take a look inside the cockpit and re-familiarise ourselves with some key components.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_pla_0: Not at all, Maddox, I'm here to learn.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_ins_3: Well, I guess that's where you differ from Harry - he always thought he knew best!
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_narrative_pla_1: Sure, whatever you think's best, Maddox.
strings.str_hsim_cockpit_intro_ins_0: Now, we'll take a look inside the cockpit, covering the essential components.
strings.str_hsim_batteries_ins_0: Find the switch which controls the electrical systems. It's on the central panel.
strings.str_hsim_batteries_ins_1: This powers the systems on and off.
strings.str_hsim_batteries_ins_2: Be aware, however, that the batteries only have a limited charge.
strings.str_hsim_missionpursuitboat_sum: Coordinate with the Coastguard and track vessels from above.
strings.str_hsim_missionpursuitboat_desc:
COASTGUARD ASSISTANCE CONTRACT

US Coast Guard Station Seattle, hereafter referred to as the CLIENT, and the CONTRACTOR hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The CLIENT requires the CONTRACTOR to provide tactical maritime support, hereafter referred to as the SERVICES. SERVICES may include the pursuit, tracking or apprehension of vessels, as per the CLIENT's direction.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT (as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.

strings.str_hsim_boat_follow_pla_1: Coast guard, we have a visual on the boat. Suspects turning eastward.
strings.str_hsim_boat_follow_pla_2: Coast guard, we have a visual on the boat. Suspects moving southward.
strings.str_hsim_boat_follow_pla_3: Coast guard, we have a visual on the boat. Suspects clipping northward.
strings.str_hsim_boat_follow_pla_4: Coast guard, be advised, suspects are firing at the helicopter!
strings.str_hsim_boat_follow_pla_5: Coast guard, be advised, boat is on fire.
strings.str_hsim_boat_detain_tec_0: Chopper one, we are code 4 on the suspects.
strings.str_hsim_boat_detain_tec_1: Chopper one, boat has been halted by force.
strings.str_hsim_boat_detain_tec_2: Chopper one, be advised, the boat has come to a halt.
strings.str_hsim_boat_dis_0: Chopper one, we have multiple 4-17s on a boat near 5-5-0. Stand by.
strings.str_hsim_boat_dis_1: Chopper one, code 3 on the 5-5-0. Suspects are in white boat, heading northward fast. Coast guard is notified.
strings.str_hsim_missionpursuit_sum: Support the SPD by tracking down fugitives on the run.
strings.str_hsim_missionpursuit_desc:
POLICE ASSISTANCE CONTRACT

Seattle Police Department, hereafter referred to as the CLIENT, and the CONTRACTOR hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The CLIENT requires the CONTRACTOR to provide police aerial support services, hereafter referred to as the SERVICES. SERVICES include the provision of assistance with the tracking and apprehension of persons of interest.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT(as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_generic_suspect_dis_0: Chopper One, we have a location of a fleeing suspect, standby.
strings.str_hsim_generic_suspect_dis_1: Chopper One, code 3 on the suspect, last known position updated. Ground units in pursuit.
strings.str_hsim_generic_suspect_pla_0: 10-4, we are code 3 on the suspect.
strings.str_hsim_generic_follow_pla_0: Ground team, suspect is heading westward.
strings.str_hsim_generic_follow_pla_1: Ground team, suspect is moving eastward.
strings.str_hsim_generic_follow_pla_2: Ground team, suspect is fleeing southward.
strings.str_hsim_generic_follow_pla_3: Ground team, suspect is heading northward.
strings.str_hsim_generic_follow_pla_4: Ground team, we've lost visual with target.
strings.str_hsim_generic_detain_tec_0: Chopper one, we have a visual.
strings.str_hsim_generic_detain_tec_1: Chopper one, we are code 4 on the suspect.
strings.str_hsim_generic_detain_tec_2: Chopper one, stand down. Suspect detained.
strings.str_hsim_missionrescue_sum: Provide emergency medical transport support using your winch-equipped helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_missionrescue_desc:
EMERGENCY SERVICES CONTRACT

The Emergency Services Department of Seattle, hereafter referred to as the CLIENT, and the CONTRACTOR hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The CLIENT requires the CONTRACTOR to provide air emergency services, hereafter referred to as the SERVICES. SERVICES include fast-response, winch-line pickup, and medical transport of patients to the closest trauma center available.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT (as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_return_pla_0: Dispatch, this is Code Blue Flight, patient is aboard, stable. We're en route back.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_return_pla_1: Dispatch, this is Code Blue Flight, patient is aboard, unstable. We'll notify you on arrival.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_return_pla_2: Dispatch, this is Code Blue Flight, patient is aboard, stable. Code Blue Flight is en route, trauma team needed.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_return_pla_3: Dispatch, this is Code Blue Flight, patient is aboard, unstable. Trauma team needed.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_patient_dis_0: Code Blue Flight, assistance needed on the crash. Patient female, probable spine or lower body injury, unconscious, vitals unknown. Land zone clear, signal white. Ground team on the way.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_patient_dis_1: Code Blue Flight, assistance needed. Patient male, leg injury, conscious, vitals stable. Land zone clear. Ground team on the way.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_patient_dis_2: Code Blue Flight, assistance needed on the incident. Patient male, probable head injury, unconscious, vitals unstable. Land zone clear. Ground team on the way.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_patient_dis_3: Code Blue Flight, assistance needed near the accident. Patient female, lower body injury, unconscious, vitals unknown. Land zone crowded, signal white. Ground team on the way.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_car_dis_0: Code Blue Flight, we have a location on car accident. Two heavily injured. Stand by.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_car_dis_1: Code Blue Flight, we have a report of a multiple car accident. Several heavily injured. Stand by.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_car_dis_2: Code Blue Flight, car incident near your location. Multiple casualties. Stand by.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_bike_dis_0: Code Blue Flight, assistance needed. We have a location on a bike crash. One heavily injured. Stand by.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_bike_dis_1: Code Blue Flight, stand by, we've got a report of a bike accident.
strings.str_hsim_generic_accident_bike_dis_2: Code Blue Flight, bike incident near your location. Possible multiple casualties. Stand by.
strings.str_hsim_missionslingload_sum: Perform slingload transport tasks across various construction projects.
strings.str_hsim_missionslingload_desc:
SLINGLOAD CONTRACT

The CONTRACTOR and the CLIENT (see below) hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The CLIENT requires slingload construction support, whereby the CONTRACTOR transports various loads, including cargo pallets, containers, and other construction materials, according to the CLIENT's requirements.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT(as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_sling_wor_1: Watch it closely. It'll swing wildly if you're not careful.
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_setdown_wor_0: Good, now place it on the spot. We'll unhook it.
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_setdown_wor_1: Closer, closer... Ok, that's it. Wait till we unhook it.
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_setdown_wor_2: Alright, head on in, we'll disconnect the load.
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_intro_wor_0: Glad you can join us! Pick it up!
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_intro_wor_1: Hey, welcome. I'll hook it up!
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_intro_wor_2: How are ya? Come to play with us? Come in lower!
strings.str_hsim_oneliners_done_wor_0: Good job, see ya next time.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_building_wor_0: Hiya, Tom, glad you can join us. Pick up the cottages one by one and place them in the right location.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_building_wor_1: Good, now place it on the spot. We'll unhook it.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_building_wor_3: Last but not least, huh? Nice job. Thanks for the help! Bye.
strings.str_hsim_missionsightseeing_sum: Pick up the CLIENT/S and give them the best tour of their lives. M.
strings.str_hsim_missionsightseeing_desc:
TRANSPORTATION AND SIGHTSEEING CONTRACT

CONTRACTOR and the CLIENT (see below) hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

CLIENT is anybody who orders SERVICES (see below) specified in this CONTRACT and agrees the terms (specified separately in ANNEX II).

SERVICES include sightseeing tours or other tours made according to CLIENT's needs.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT(as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_stadiums_pla_0: Here's the famous football stadium where many a fine game's been played.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_stadiums_pla_1: The stadium was finished in 2002 and cost over $430 million.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_stadiums_pla_2: It's also known to be loudest stadium in States, sometimes giving the opposing team players trouble hearing each other.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_stadiums_pla_3: It has an all-seater capacity of 72'000.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_stadiums_pla_4: Visiting kickers hate this place, with strong winds coming in from across the bay.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_stadiums_pla_5: You can also see the famous baseball stadium close by it. This one cost $518 million and has capacity of 48'000.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_stadiums_pla_6: It's got a unique retractable roof, and only one other baseball stadium in the world can boast that.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_spaceneedle_pla_0: The Space Needle. It was built for the 1962 World's Fair.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_spaceneedle_pla_1: With a height of 184m- though, only six floors - it's become a major landmark in Seattle.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_spaceneedle_pla_2: Inside the rotating crown sits a restaurant, which was originally orange, but people didn't like it so much.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_spaceneedle_pla_3: Close by to the needle you can see a couple of nice architectural piece. The 'Experience Music Project' and th Science Fiction Museum.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_spaceneedle_pla_4: The nearby museum was designed by Frank Gehry, and it's believed to be in the shape of smashed guitar body as a tribute to Jimmy Hendrix.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_pugetsound_pla_0: What you can see right here is Puget Sound.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_pugetsound_pla_1: It's definitions are many, but simply enough said, it's a complex coastal body of water with a system of interconnected marine waterways and basins.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_pugetsound_pla_2: It was explored by George Vancouver in 1792.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_pugetsound_pla_3: Also, Puget Sound is the name of this region and during WWII it was a war industry heaven.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_lakewashington_pla_0: We're now just flying above Lake Washington.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_lakewashington_pla_1: It's the largest lake in King County and surrounds Mercer Island.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_lakewashington_pla_2: Mercer Island is a city and the most populated island in the US.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_lakewashington_pla_3: Just a few weeks ago, it was a big part of the Blue Angels air display during Seattle's summer Seafair celebration.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_downtown_pla_0: We're close to the two famous skyscrapers: the Columbia Centre and Smith Tower.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_downtown_pla_1: The Columbia Center was completed in '85 with a height of 294m. It counts 76 floors of A-class offices, making it the tallest skyscraper in Seattle.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_downtown_pla_2: Smith Tower is the oldest one. It was finished in 1914 and is named after its builder, Lyman Cornelius Smith. Up until 1931 it was the tallest office building west of the Mississippi River.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_downtown_pla_3: The Smith Tower has 38 floors and even includes a fallout shelter, which can be seen from entrance hall.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_boeingfactory_pla_0: This is the Boeing Everett Factory.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_boeingfactory_pla_1: It's the largest building in the world by volume at approximately 13.4 million cubic meters.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_boeingfactory_pla_2: Boeing 747s, 767s, 777s and 787s Dreamliner are all built here.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_boeingfactory_pla_3: Across the airport to the west is The Boeing Store, a theatre, and Future of Flight Aviation Centre & Boeing Tour, which runs factory tours.
strings.str_hsim_01_intro_pla_0: Welcome to our flight. Today, I'll be taking you through some interesting places in this city.
strings.str_hsim_01_intro_pla_1: Welcome. Today you'll experience a tour of Seattle.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_valve_pla_0: If you're into games you will like our next view.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_valve_pla_1: As you can see we are just passing above Valve offices. The makers of famous Half Life and founders of Steam.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_valve_pla_2: Gabe Newell and Mike Harrington founded Valve on 1996, they moved here in 2003 after incorporation.
strings.str_hsim_landmark_valve_pla_3: The computer games industry is projected to be worth worth over fifty billion dollars annually!
strings.str_hsim_missionvisitgolf_sum: Transport the CLIENT and circle the required golf courses.
strings.str_hsim_missionvisitgolf_desc:
TRANSPORTATION CONTRACT

The CONTRACTOR and CLIENT hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement, hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The CLIENT requires transportation to observe various golf courses(cf. flight plan). Transport the CLIENT to the specified courses, and circle the location.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT (as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_golf_gol_0: We'll by doing some golf course fly-bys today.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_golf_gol_1: There's the one. Nice course, 18 holes. That 3 par looks dangerous!
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_golf_gol_2: Goodness me, this one is 9 hole. Y'know, these Americans have taken our noble sport and done some terrible things to it.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_golf_gol_3: Now this is what I've been talking about. Give us another turn about would'ya?
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_golf_gol_4: Ok, that's enough. Take me back. And light a fire under it - I've got a taste for the nineteenth hole!
strings.str_hsim_missionvisit_sum: Transport the CLIENT and circle the required locations.
strings.str_hsim_missionvisit_desc:
TRANSPORTATION CONTRACT

The CONTRACTOR and CLIENT hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement, hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The CLIENT requires transportation to observe various locations (cf. flight plan). Transport the CLIENT to their requested destination, and circle the location.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT (as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_property_buy_0: I need you to show me some properties. Please follow the map you have been supplied with!
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_property_buy_1: Very good! Hold it steady a while longer: I'd like to take some photos.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_property_buy_2: There it is. My, this place looks very nice, wouldn't you agree?
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_property_buy_3: Ah, you've found it. They're asking a good deal of money here, y'know. And for what? For this? Get me out of here.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_property_buy_4: Another one. Lemme see. Could you fly a little lower? I would like to take a closer look.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_property_buy_5: I like the view from up here. I should've been a pilot.
strings.str_hsim_01_oneliners_property_buy_6: That'd be all for today! Thank you for the flight! Take me back please.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_sum:
Just to confirm, I'll pick you up and we'll take the scenic route back to Highland Park Heliport.

Looking forward to it, bro.

J.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_9: T:Sorry, bro. What happened - it sure was one hell of mess.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_7: J:base of the spine. looks like its gonna stay that way for the foreseeable...
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_6: J:nothing new -- back is still a mess
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_4: T:You've been to see the specialist, or... no?
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_17: T:Sure, thanks for your support, bro. It's appreciated.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_16: J:well I've got paperwork to sort out -- get u up n running with some contracts soon enuf
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_14: J:u think I'd leave u behind to fix up this business all by urself? %1
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_im_11: T:I'm just glad you made it out
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_desc:
Hey, Bro,
It's great that you're able to spare the time to come visit. Dad's service was a chance for the whole family to get together; honestly, it reminded me just how close we used to be, and how we're a little more disconnected now, y'know?

Right now, I'm still busy sorting through all the paperwork that dad left behind, but the plan is for me to pick you up in one of the choppers - I'm looking forward to getting back up in the air with you!

Maybe we'll take a short tour of Downtown - get at look at Highland Park heliport from the air - then we'll grab some food with the rest of the guys! Really looking forward to seeing, man.

Best, Joe.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_intro_briefing.html_6: As your brother dropped you off, his helicopter suffered a horrible crash.
strings.str_hsim_event_landing_bro_1: Alright, bro', I shouldn't be very long...
strings.str_hsim_event_landing_bro_2: Meet and greet with the guys and, hey, at least try to save me one beer!
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_2_b_bro_0: Hey, tell you what, let's try again - don't even think about last time.
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_2_b_bro_1: Take the controls and just try a simple bank out towards the water...
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_2_b_bro_2: Just relax. Take your time. Slow, careful adjustments to the controls, brother.
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_2_a_bro_0: Hey, fancy another shot, Tom? You seem to be able to handle it just fine.
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_2_a_bro_1: Let's try a simple bank - out towards the water, maybe?
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_2_a_bro_2: Try to get a good feel for the weight of the thing...
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_1_bro_0: Hey now, here's an idea... What'd'ya think about taking the controls?
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_1_bro_1: Y'know, just a quick spin! Get the feel of the thing again, yeah?
strings.str_hsim_task_takeover_1_bro_2: Hey, don't look at me like that! It'll be fine, I promise.
strings.str_hsim_feedback_2_good_bro_1: Awesome. Really, it's great to have you up here with me.
strings.str_hsim_feedback_2_bad_bro_1: Ok, just try... uh - keep her stable - small adjustments.
strings.str_hsim_feedback_1_good_bro_0: Hey, not bad... not bad at all!
strings.str_hsim_feedback_1_good_bro_1: See? You never forget, Tom. Just like riding a bike, right?
strings.str_hsim_feedback_1_good_bro_2: Except, y'know, with rotor-blades, and - or, no, is it more like a horse - ah, forget it - I'm babbling now!
strings.str_hsim_feedback_1_bad_bro_0: Ok, ok, easy now, Tom, easy...
strings.str_hsim_feedback_1_bad_bro_1: Just try to get her straight and level, if you can...
strings.str_hsim_event_takeback_2_bro_1: Ok, I'll take her from here again...
strings.str_hsim_event_takeback_2_bro_2: So, uh, maybe we can make one more pass around Downtown if you'd like?
strings.str_hsim_event_takeback_1_bro_0: Alright, bro', great job, I'll take her from here.
strings.str_hsim_event_takeback_1_bro_1: Good, I've got her now, bro'.
strings.str_hsim_event_takeback_1_bro_2: Ok, I'll take us along the shoreline, you should be able to get a decent view of Downtown from there.
strings.str_hsim_event_mayday_com_0: Mayday, mayday, mayday, this is cargo ship Xiamijn; break.
strings.str_hsim_event_mayday_com_1: Location: Puget Sound; I am a cargo ship damaged and sinking with ten crew aboard.
strings.str_hsim_event_mayday_com_2: I Require immediate assistance. Mayday, Xiamijn, over.
strings.str_hsim_event_mayday_dis_0: Uh, vessel Xiamijn, this is Coast Guard Station Seattle Medical. Dispatching rescue boats to your position, stand by.
strings.str_hsim_event_introduction_bro_0: Yup, looks like a storm's gathering... little earlier than forecast, though.
strings.str_hsim_event_introduction_bro_1: ...If there's one thing that's supposed to be predictable here, it's the rain, right?
strings.str_hsim_event_handover_1_bro_0: Alright, then! You've got the controls, Tom'...
strings.str_hsim_event_handover_1_bro_1: Ok, Just hold a straight and level path...
strings.str_hsim_event_handover_1_bro_2: Remember, like dad always used to say: fly the attitude...
strings.str_hsim_ambient_rtb_bro_0: Alright, Tom, I'm afraid we'll have to cut this one short.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_rtb_bro_1: We've got a search light bolted onto this chopper. I'm gonna try and put it to good use.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_rtb_bro_2: I'll drop you off at the heliport - Highland Park's just a few minutes away now.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_3_com_0: Coast Guard Seattle, Xiamijn; go ahead, over.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_3_dis_0: Vessel Xiamijn, this is Coast Guard Station Seattle Medical. Message, over.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_3_dis_1: Vessel Xiamijn, we have, uh, two rescue helicopters en route to your position. ETA five minutes.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_2_dis_0: Code Blue Flight, understood. What is your ETA, over?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_2_dis_1: Code Blue Flight, Code Green Flight en route.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_2_med_0: Dispatch, this is Code Blue Flight, en route to the location; over.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_2_dis_2: Roger, Code Blue. We're struggling to redirect now; will keep you updated; out.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_2_med_1: Dispatch, uh... ETA five minutes. Any other helicopters en route? Over.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_2_med_2: Dispatch, uh, that's it? Reports indicate it's a total mess; over.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_1_com_0: Coast Guard Seattle, understood. We've got one seriously injured here, over.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_1_dis_0: Vessel Xiamijn, Be advised, rescue boats are dispatched; ETA, uh, ten minutes; over.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_mayday_1_dis_1: Roger, Xiamijn; trauma team on standby.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_landed_mec_2: Kelly, get help! Kelly, it's Joe, quickly, get help!
strings.str_hsim_ambient_dad_bro_0: Y'know, I'd gotten to thinking... it's been a while since dad took you up for your lessons.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_dad_bro_1: God, it's almost six years, right? Half a decade - can you believe that?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_chat_bro_0: It's great to have you up here, bro'. Really, it is.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_chat_bro_1: And, honestly, since dad passed, it's been a real struggle on my own.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_chat_bro_2: With this economy, it's just way too tight to hire another pilot, y'know?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_chat_bro_3: I guess what I'm sayin' is - I dunno - it's just real great to see you again, Tom.
strings.str_hsim_us_c_01_sum: Meet Marty at the needle and follow his lead. M.
strings.str_hsim_04_cancel_pio_0: Understood. Tom, this is Partridge. Police are all over the place. This job is cancelled while we wait for things to calm down.
strings.str_hsim_04_cancel_pio_1: Get down with the antenna immediately and return it back where you got it.
strings.str_hsim_04_cancel_wor_0: Hold up, boss, we've got some protesters or something sanding on the Space Needle. One of them looks set to base-jump or something.
strings.str_hsim_04_cancel_pio_2: Sorry, Tom, of course you'll receive full payment, though it looks like I can't get no satisfaction today. Bunch of show-offs.
strings.str_hsim_03_got_it_pla_0: Alright, load attached. Where should I drop it?
strings.str_hsim_03_got_it_wor_0: Great work. The old scrapyard at the north edge of the town. Do you know it?
strings.str_hsim_03_got_it_wor_1: Also, be sure to count on the sling waving about. When you stop too quickly your load will wave like a see-saw. Got that, bumpkin?
strings.str_hsim_03_got_it_wor_2: Drop the load there and get the new one.
strings.str_hsim_02_needle_pla_0: Uh, sure. I got it, old timer.
strings.str_hsim_02_needle_wor_0: What'cha waiting for, boy? Get close so we can start working.
strings.str_hsim_02_needle_wor_1: Now, look: the antenna will be hooked to the synthetic web we prepared. Once your in place, the antenna will slowly fall into a laying position.
strings.str_hsim_02_needle_wor_2: Do that, and you're free to go.
strings.str_hsim_02_needle_wor_3: The load is light, so don't worry, but... the maximum angle of the leg is 40 degrees - so be careful on those, uh... brakes.
strings.str_hsim_02_needle_wor_4: He's alright that kid. Ok, slowly head up and fly safe.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_man_1: Tom, this is Mr. Howard Partridge from Partridge Inc. Mr. Partridge has a job for us.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_man_2: It's a prestigious task and we really need him to be satisfied.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_man_3: Don't worry, Tom. It's a tough job, but we really need it.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pio_0: Because, my dear boy, I'm in something of a rush and I'm sitting on a pile of money.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pla_1: Nice to meet you, sir, and why might I satisfy you today?
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pio_1: I know when and where to pull the strings; I can be a very useful man to know.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pio_2: The Space Needle needs a new antenna. It's sling load job. Now, I know you've never done it before, but that's of little consequence.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pla_2: Of course, sir. What's this job about?
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pio_3: See - as far as I know - nobody's ever done it before. And you'll work with the best men I can offer.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pio_4: The workers are already on site at the Needle. Good luck Tom - glad you could join us.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pla_3: Ok, I'll do it. Let's just hope I don't screw it up - this is The Needle after all.
strings.str_hsim_01_job_pla_4: So, let do it. Where should I go?
strings.str_hsim_us_c_01_desc:
PARTRIDGE CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT

Partridge Construction, hereafter referred to as the CLIENT, and the CONTRACTOR hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The CLIENT requires the CONTRACTOR to repair the Space Needle antenna .

The CONTRACTOR requires swift completion of the job at time and date specified in the ANNEX I.

Failure to execute the terms of the CONTRACT(as defined separately in Annex II) will result in termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_sum:
Just to confirm, I'm heading across now to pick you up now.

We'll drive up to HPH together, so I can formally introduce you to the rest of the team, and see about getting you some extra training.

J.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_8: J:exactly -- ur safety is my first priority tombo
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_7: T:Sure, yeah. Hopefully I can get started on some simpler tasks first, though - get me up to speed.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_6: J:real looking forward to getting things moving around here, yknow?
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_3: T:Yeah, they seem like a gddbunch of guys!
strings.str_hsim_event_radio_intro_new_0: ... and finally, the battle surrounding the Xiamijn cargo disaster rumbled on today.
strings.str_hsim_event_radio_intro_new_1: Fierce exchanges took place between police and activists, amid a series of meetings between Vrana Corp representatives and state officials.
strings.str_hsim_event_radio_intro_new_2: I'm Don Kinsley, those were the headlines on the hour. You're listening to 97.1, KBBC-attle Radio: tune it, in turn it up, and rip off that knob.
strings.str_hsim_event_radio_intro_new_3: Coming up next we've got sports-beat, right after these messages...
strings.str_hsim_event_brother_intro_bro_1: Hey, Tommy... c'mon, bro', we're almost here.
strings.str_hsim_event_brother_intro_bro_2: Look, man, you've got nothing to worry about. Seriously. Without you, we'd be dead already - dead in the water.
strings.str_hsim_05_intro_tutorials_bro_0: First things first - we need to bring you up to speed, Tom.
strings.str_hsim_05_intro_tutorials_bro_1: I've arranged for an instructor to come help brush up your skills.
strings.str_hsim_05_intro_tutorials_pla_0: Uh, where do we begin, Joey? How do we dig ourselves out of this one?
strings.str_hsim_05_intro_tutorials_bro_2: You just have to make the call; the number's in the office.
strings.str_hsim_04_intro_team_bro_0: Tom, this is Paul Kelly. He handles security for us, infact, he's handled most of the goings-on here since...
strings.str_hsim_04_intro_team_bro_1: And this is Andrew, he's our maintenance manager. Craymer here knows as much about these birds as anyone I've ever met.
strings.str_hsim_04_intro_team_mec_0: Hey, how you doing? Yeah, it's sure great to meet you, Tom. That's a fact.
strings.str_hsim_04_intro_team_sec_0: A pleasure to formally meet you, son. It's 'Kelly' - you can call me 'Kelly'.
strings.str_hsim_04_intro_team_sec_1: I knew your father for years, son. He was a great man - and your brother here, too.
strings.str_hsim_04_intro_team_mec_1: We need to get things moving around here. Back on track. Your brother speaks highly of you. Very highly.
strings.str_hsim_04_intro_team_pla_0: Uh, thanks, guys, it's... it's good to finally be here. You're right, we have a lot of work to do.
strings.str_hsim_03_intro_goals_bro_0: We've got one or two weeks left, tops. You'll be fine. We'll take on some simple jobs. Ease you in.
strings.str_hsim_03_intro_goals_bro_1: We're gonna get through this, Tom. You know that. Together.
strings.str_hsim_03_intro_goals_pla_0: Yeah, you're right Joe... you're right.
strings.str_hsim_02_intro_brothers_bro_0: We've got one last chance, y'know? We've got to seize it - we owe it to dad; this business was his life - it's our future.
strings.str_hsim_02_intro_brothers_bro_1: It's fine. I like it just fine.
strings.str_hsim_02_intro_brothers_bro_2: That's... not what's important right now. The accident happened; we accept that and we move on.
strings.str_hsim_02_intro_brothers_pla_0: 'Tom Larkin: helicopter pilot'... I'm not so sure, Joey, does that have a ring to it?
strings.str_hsim_02_intro_brothers_pla_1: I'm sorry. It's just - it is a lot of pressure. You were the one like dad - always around the choppers - you lived and breathed it.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_13: J:lol. cmon tombo. im only messing with you! %1
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_11: J:hey hey less talking about backs - mines still killing me!
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_10: T:Thanks, bro. I know you've always got my back.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_im_1: J:hey tombo. so -- what do u think of the team?
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_01_desc:
Hey, Tom, I hope all's well.
So, I've discussed with the rest of the team about you coming to help us out. Suffice to say, they're all real keen to get you on board.

I'll drive us up to Highland Park Heliport as soon as I can get a break in my schedule. We're in a bit of a mess right now - that's only to be expected after dad, and now my accident - and I know you've got your reservations, but this is the right move.

I'll call an old pal of dad's - he's a flight instructor - and find out when he's available to help you brush up on your skills.

Best, Joe.
strings.str_hsim_us_g_p2_01_sum:
Meet Henderson at the airfield and stay safe. This is serious work.
K.

strings.str_hsim_us_g_01_briefing.html_8: S.W.A.T. arrested all suspects after the fast-rope insertion.
strings.str_hsim_us_g_01_briefing.html_3: The fast-rope insertion took too long.
strings.str_hsim_us_g_01_briefing.html_1: Your helicopter was spotted by the suspects too soon.
