strings.str_hsim_06_event_shotdown_mil_0: Battlemage to Whisky-6, copy that. Dispatching CSAR to your location, over.
strings.str_hsim_05_event_drop_01_cop_0: Line her up carefully; reduce your airspeed on approach.
strings.str_hsim_05_event_drop_01_cop_1: We want an even spread; try to keep your airspeed consistent. I'll release the payload on your command.
strings.str_hsim_04_mil_task_start_bro_0: Battlemage, Whisky-6; copy that: clear for take-off; heading north-east. Whisky-6.
strings.str_hsim_04_mil_task_start_mil_0: Whiskey-6, this is Battlemage: you are cleared for take-off. Exit north-east, over.
strings.str_hsim_04_mil_start_bro_0_0: We were tasked to fly checkpoint-to-check-point, distributing information leaflets about what'd happened... about the future of the country.
strings.str_hsim_04_mil_start_bro_1: The 'democratic process', y'know, all that kinda junk.
strings.str_hsim_03_mil_intro_bro_0_0: Well, it was post-invasion - we'd ripped through whatever 'standing-army' had existed - all key positions were under coalition control.
strings.str_hsim_03_mil_intro_bro_1_0: Only a guerilla insurgency remained, and what was most important was to get the local population on our side.
strings.str_hsim_02b_brother_later_pla_0_0: Sure, I can understand that, Joey.
strings.str_hsim_02b_brother_later_pla_1_0: I know that you need your space sometimes. I'll catch up with you later, ok?
strings.str_hsim_02a_brother_continue_bro_0_0: I know, Tom. In fact, it was something about your flight, me getting the paperwork... I know it'll sound stupid...
strings.str_hsim_02a_brother_continue_pla_0_0: You know, if it helps you get it off your chest, I'm always here - it's healthy to open up about things.
strings.str_hsim_02a_brother_continue_pla_1: Not at all, man. Please, go on.
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_bro_0_0: Oh, Tom, sorry - God, I was a million miles away - just, emailing some guys from way back, y'know...
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_bro_1_0: Oh, right, yeah - how was the flight?
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_pla_0_0: Sure can get a bit warm in here, huh, Joe?
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_bro_2_0: Oh, Tom, I'm sorry, my head - it's all over the place right now - the meds, y'know, they, sometimes...
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_pla_2: Sure, sure, Bro'... Hey, um, we have some things to discuss. Mr Haydon, he -
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_bro_3_0: No, no, you misunderstand. Mr Haydon faxed across some documents while you were in the air; I'm aware of their proposal.
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_pla_3: The flight itself was fine, it's more - uh - actually, what he had to say that was of interest.
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_bro_4: Yeah, yeah.. I'm fine. I've just, I dunno, lately, I've been thinking a lot about back when I was flying.
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_pla_4: Sure, Joe, no worries. I can explain it more, uh, slowly..?
strings.str_hsim_01_core_outro_pla_5: Oh... oh, right, sure... Hey, is everything ok, Joe?
strings.str_hsim_us_mil_03_desc:
Operation Bullseye is in effect. The bulk of the enemy's standing army has capitulated, leaving only a tough kernel of the Republic die-hard, who have splintered into fractious guerilla groups, distributed in pockets across the region.

This new insurgency warfare has proven a challenge to conventional tactics. Command has authorised a new strategy, and as part of that, we need to get the bulk of the peaceful local population on board.

You're tasked to distribute information leaflets across several key locations, as part of the broader 'hearts and minds' campaign.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_05_sum:
Direct fast-response units to where the materials are warehoused.
M.C.
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_ceo_ceo_0: What on earth is going on here?
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_ceo_ceo_2: I know it's you, Larkin - back away, now!
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_ceo_ceo_3: You've got no idea what you're getting involved in here!
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_ceo_ceo_4: This is your last chance to back off, Tom...
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_ceo_ceo_5: Mark my words, you've just made a big mistake.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_bro_1: So, do we even know what happened? Do you have any more information than us?
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_bro_2: I'm just glad they didn't charge you. Honestly - it's been crazy here.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_pla_0: Thanks bro', it's good to be home.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_bro_3: Whatever the case, I'm just glad your a free man. That was a crazy stunt you pulled.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_sec_0: Honestly, Joe, seems like no one's got any info at the moment.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_sec_1: Even my buddies on the force say this goes way over their heads...
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_bro_4: In fact, later today I have a meeting with a new executive about returning control of Larkin Aviation to us.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_bro_5: But, we might just see about keeping on a few of their staff.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_bro_6: ...Seems a business manager can have its advantages, right Michelle?
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_bro_7: Yeah, it's early days, Tom, but let's just see about getting Larkin Aviation back on course. We've got a lot to Take On.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_pla_1: Well, the authorities weren't exactly clear on the details, but - as you've probably heard - they're holding Haydon.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_pla_2: Seems to me like whatever it was we were looking for, he was trying take out of the country with him.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_man_0: He's right. There have been police all over the heliport. But it's great to have you back.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_pla_3: Yeah, I know - I sure hope Maddox doesn�t find out about it.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_man_1: He's right, actually. They're scrambling all over the place. Trying to distance themselves from the whole affair.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_mec_0: The important thing is, Haydon's under investigation, and Vrana itself is taking some real heat about the whole cargo incident.
strings.str_hsim_core_outro_mec_1: It's no less than they deserve, that's a fact.
strings.str_hsim_radio_outro_new_0: It's crazy times in Seattle, with an executive of one of the state's largest companies and employers under federal investigation on as yet undisclosed charges.
strings.str_hsim_radio_outro_new_1: Vrana Corp have been unavailable for comment over the weekend, with business analysts keeping a close eye on their stock with the opening of the markets in just a few hours.
strings.str_hsim_radio_outro_new_2: I'm Don Kinsley, those were the headlines on the hour. You're listening to 97.1, KBBC-attle Radio: tune it, in turn it up, and rip off that knob!
strings.str_hsim_task_takeoff_sec_0: Alright, Tom, take us up to the compound.
strings.str_hsim_task_takeoff_sec_1: The team will fast-rope in - keep Vrana Corp from making any sudden moves.
strings.str_hsim_task_land_pla_0: Do you think they'll find it?
strings.str_hsim_task_land_sec_1: No word from the ground team, though - hell, there must be a lot of containers.
strings.str_hsim_task_land_sec_2: I dunno, son, but, honestly, it doesn't seem like we have enough time just to sit around and find out...
strings.str_hsim_task_land_sec_3: Set us down, we'll direct them to it.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_pla_1: Right. Then I need to stop him. Any way I can.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_sec_0: Tom, I've got a call from Michelle.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_pla_2: You stay here - there's got to be something for us to go on. Find it.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_sec_1: No, it's Haydon. That tail number checked out. She's confirmed the airport.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_sec_2: He's... due to leave any time now, Tom, I'm sorry.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_sec_3: Unless we have some evidence, the cops just aren't going to do anything to stop him.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_pla_3: It'll be over once I've stopped him.
strings.str_hsim_task_ceo_leaving_sec_4: Now just hold on Tom, what are you thinking? Look, it's over - I'm sorry.
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_incorrect_swa_0: Nope! C'mon let's move - going to check that one!
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_incorrect_swa_2: Damn, nothing. We're moving to check the last one.
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_incorrect_swa_3: Alright, have we got something over here?
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_hints_pla_2: C'mon... it's gotta be here somewhere.
strings.str_hsim_event_rush_man_0: Tom, you need to know: Mr Haydon is leaving right now.
strings.str_hsim_event_rush_man_1: You've got to move quickly if you want to stop him from leaving.
strings.str_hsim_event_dropoff_sec_1: Hold her steady while the team ropes in!
strings.str_hsim_event_discovery_pla_0: Hey, I found it - over here!
strings.str_hsim_event_discovery_pla_1: No... no, this can't be right - it's empty.
strings.str_hsim_event_discovery_swa_0: Goddamnit. Look, I'm just about done here. I'm not wasting any more of my boys' time on it.
strings.str_hsim_event_discovery_swa_1: Look, son, I dunno know what kind of Hollywood trash you think this is, but Vrana is a respectable company.
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_pla_0: Kelly? I've stopped him! I've stopped Haydon! Do you have anything at your end?
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_pla_1: What do you mean? You have nothing?
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_pla_2: Ok, I suppose that's good news? Ok, ok. Maybe.. maybe call our lawyer though, huh?
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_sec_1: But, one of the security guards here had some very interesting information.
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_sec_2: Nothing tangible... but get this: Haydon was here a few hours ago.
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_sec_3: Just him and one assistant. Shady looking fella'. Apparently, they loaded up some SUV and sped away.
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_sec_4: All very shady. It's not much, no, but the SWAT guys think it's enough to talk to Haydon. So just sit tight.
strings.str_hsim_event_ceo_stopped_sec_5: Oh, don't worry, Tom. He's already been notified!
strings.str_hsim_ambient_brother_advice_bro_0: Tom, it's your brother here. Kelly just told me your plan.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_brother_advice_bro_1: You don't need to do this, Tom.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_brother_advice_bro_2: Look, it's just not worth risking your life.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_brother_advice_bro_3: For God's sake... be careful Tom.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_brother_advice_pla_0: No, Joey, I do. I've got a feeling about this.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_brother_advice_pla_1: I appreciate your concern, bro', but I know what I'm doing.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_man_0_0: Tom, you're back - how's your brother?
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_man_1_0: Ok, that is a relief. But what now? What are you going to do?
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_man_2_0: Well, if there is any evidence to be found, it's locked away at the Hood Complex.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_pla_0_0_1: As well as can be expected, thanks.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_pla_1: He should be back on his feet in the next few days.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_man_3: You've got to move quickly. Mr Haydon is due to leave the country today.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_sec_0_0: I've been in contact with a buddy on the force. He says command is dragging their feet over this one.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_sec_1_0: They say there's no basis for an investigation.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_mec_0_0: Oh, well that is bull. We haven't got much, no - but we got something - that's a fact. Gotta be foul play.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_sec_2: For once, Craymer, I'd have to agree with you.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_mec_1_0: In the mean time, I'll head over to the hospital. Joe will want to know the situation, that's for sure.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_sec_3: We got one shot. My buddy agreed to deploy a response team, he just doesn't have the logistics.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_sec_4: If we can direct them to whatever it is that they have in there, they won't have a choice but to move on Haydon.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_sec_5: I'll come up with you, Tom - liaise with the police team.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_05_im_2: T:I just did the same thing as you would have done, Joe. This is our city; this is our business - no one's taking that away from us.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_05_desc:
Hey, Tom. This is it. Our last chance is to direct the authorities towards whatever it is they have stashed away at the Hood Warehouse Complex.

We know that they aren't going to remain out in the open for much longer, but the police just don't have the resources to move quickly enough. It seems that we've got to act now.

Kelly's put a word in with some old friends on the force. Transport and direct a response team directly to wherever the containers are stored.

Good luck, Tom.
Michelle.

strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_sum:
Fly across to the Veteran's Memorial and perform the manoeuvres required for the show!

J.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_9: S:Don't you worry about it, son1
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_6: T:Like I say, I'm real sorry, sir.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_5: T:I was already on my way over when our owner diverted me to their 'priority task'...
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_4: T:Look, I've really got to apologise about letting you down at such short notice.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_23: -:Your message will be delivered when the receiver is online.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_22: T:Thanks, Nichols. It means a lot! Hope you have more luck with your connection!
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_20: S:- damn, Tom. We're just all glad you made it through unhurt.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_19: S:That business with your chopper today
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_18: S:No, Tom, you've said quite enough, and from what I've heard, been through enough too.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_16: T:Hah, hey, it happens to the best of us, Nichols.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_13: S:Honestly, this thing must be older then what they used to send man to the moon1
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_im_10: S:Sorry, I can hardly get this dammned contraption to type1
strings.str_hsim_event_radio_intro_new_0_0_1: ...so, the fallout from the Xiamijn disaster reached a climax yesterday with environmental activists blockading major routes around Downtown Seattle.
strings.str_hsim_event_radio_intro_new_1_0_1: Unhappy with the perceived lack of action from state officials, blockades targeted the major business centres, including the Vrana Corp Tower.
strings.str_hsim_event_radio_intro_new_2_0_1: The protests were disbanded earlier this morning, with transport officials expecting no additional delays, besides those already planned for the veterans' parade.
strings.str_hsim_task_cargo_man_0: Ok. You're to fly to the cargo wreck.
strings.str_hsim_task_cargo_man_1: It's been updated. You�ll assist in the cleanup operation.
strings.str_hsim_task_cargo_man_2: Once you're at the location, you'll be coordinating with the ground crew.
strings.str_hsim_task_cargo_pla_0: What exactly are my tasks? Where's the flight plan?
strings.str_hsim_task_cargo_man_3: Look - sorry about all this - I got a call from Mr Haydon himself...
strings.str_hsim_task_drop_1_pmc_1: Move it back to the compound and unload it there.
strings.str_hsim_task_drop_1_pmc_2: What are you waiting for a kiss goodbye? Get a move on, Larking!
strings.str_hsim_event_overwight_man_0: Hi, Tom, it's Michelle. Mr Haydon assures me that it's fine.
strings.str_hsim_event_overwight_man_1: He's serious about this one. Just... try to get the job done, ok?
strings.str_hsim_event_overwight_pla_0: Ground team, this load is too heavy. I'm getting all sorts of warnings up here.
strings.str_hsim_event_overwight_pmc_0: Oh, come on Larking, you've got your orders.
strings.str_hsim_event_overwight_pla_1: Seriously, this weight in in breach of regulations. It may damage the chopper.
strings.str_hsim_event_overwight_pmc_1: That's right, Larking, now shift it!
strings.str_hsim_event_cargo_pmc_1: Right, we need you to sling several container-loads back to the compound.
strings.str_hsim_event_cargo_pmc_2: Bring the chopper in position over here. Think you can manage that?
strings.str_hsim_task_switch_man_0: You're to divert to the Hood Warehouse Complex.
strings.str_hsim_task_switch_man_1: This task requires a special heavy-lifting helicopter. Land at the compound and switch.
strings.str_hsim_task_switch_man_2: They're expecting you. I'll provide more information in due course.
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_3_man_0: Again, I'm really sorry about all this.
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_3_man_1: No, it's understandable. This is the last load - regular weight.
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_3_man_2: If you're quick, you might still even make it to the veteran's parade...
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_3_pla_0: Sure. I appreciate it, but - honestly, Michelle - this leaves a bad taste.
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_3_man_3: Ok. Sorry again. In the mean time. I'll... I'll see what this was all about.
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_2_pmc_0: Good. Now get back to the cargo ship.
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_2_pmc_1: C'mon, we haven't got all day!
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_1_pmc_0: Alright - prep for the first load.
strings.str_hsim_task_pickup_1_pmc_1: Get into a low hover over the first container.
strings.str_hsim_task_drop_2_pmc_1: Alright, you're hooked up - try not to destroy anything else, eh?
strings.str_hsim_event_failure_dis_0: Lima Alpha Four Two... ah, roger, what is the nature of your problem?
strings.str_hsim_event_failure_dis_1: Lima Alpha Four Two, Understood. Notifying emergency services.
strings.str_hsim_event_failure_pla_1: Mayday, mayday, mayday; this is Lima Alpha Four Two, Lima Alpha Four Two. Break.
strings.str_hsim_event_failure_pla_2: Engine failure; autorotating to the ground; one man aboard; over.
strings.str_hsim_event_emergency_landed_bro_0: Thank goodness for that. Tom, shut down the systems. Stay where you are. I'll get you recovered.
strings.str_hsim_event_emergency_landed_bro_1: The blame lies squarely at Vrana Corp's door.
strings.str_hsim_event_divert_man_1: I'm afraid I'm going to have to divert you to a priority task.
strings.str_hsim_event_divert_man_2: You're to divert immediately and assist with sling-load operations for Vrana Corp.
strings.str_hsim_event_divert_man_3: I'm sorry, Tom, but there's really no room for discussion. This comes straight from the top.
strings.str_hsim_event_divert_pla_0: Hold on, what? 'Divert'? No... no, I'm already en route to the Veterans Parade...
strings.str_hsim_event_bird_strike_man_0: What was that? Is everything ok?
strings.str_hsim_event_bird_strike_pla_1: God - yeah, fine - just... bird stike.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_sorry_bro_1_0: No, you're kidding? Tom, I'm sorry. I'll talk to Carmichael.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_sorry_pla_0_0: Hi, Joe? I'm not making it to the Vet show.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_sorry_bro_2_0: Of course. No problem. Fly safe, bro'.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_sorry_pla_1_0: It's Vrana Corp. They say I have to scrap my plans and assist them.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_sorry_pla_2: It doesn't sound like there's much you can do. Just... call Nichols for me, ok?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_sorry_pla_3: Let him know the situation, and... and that I'm real sorry.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_rtb_bro_0_0: This is unacceptable, Tom. Is everything ok up there?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_rtb_bro_1_0: Good, get back asap. There's gonna be fallout from this.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_rtb_pla_0: Yeah, I'm fine - final load now.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_overweight_bro_0: Tom, I've been informed of the situation. Be very careful.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_overweight_bro_1: Be mindful of your speed. Watch the load doesn't fly you.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_overweight_bro_2: Just give yourself a little extra room with everything - particularly on approach.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_failure_bro_0: Tom, Just stay calm! Remember your procedures.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_failure_bro_1: Collective fully down; throttle to idle.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_failure_bro_2: Smooth glide down; don't let the nose dip.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_failure_bro_3: Flare to neutralise airspeed before landing.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_argument_bro_0: Just what the hell did you have my brother doing up there?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_argument_bro_1: It's unacceptable, Carmichael! What could possibly justify it?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_argument_bro_2: I want answers, not apologies! Just what the hell was going on?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_argument_man_0: I know, look: we were within our rights to get Tom to divert - but, but - Yes. The heavy load. That's... I'm sorry about that.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_argument_man_1: Look, you have every right to be angry. I'm very sorry.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_argument_man_2: I don't know. Something was wrong. I'll do some digging, I promise.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_argument_man_3: And, if you can hear this, Tom. I am sorry. I'll do everything I can.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_bro_0: Well, today's the day, Tombo! You all fired up for the Vet' show?
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_bro_1: Good to hear. Y'know... I'm real proud of you, Tom. You've come a long way.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_bro_2_0: I'd give anything to be up there myself, but, I know you'll do a great job.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_pla_0: Sure am, and Nichols is a real decent guy. Honestly, I'm glad to help out.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_bro_3_0: Actually, uh, I'll be away - I need to go to the hospital.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_bro_4_0: Yeah, y'know, well enough... I just need an assessment. Renew my prescription.
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_pla_2: Oh, but, you're ok though, right?
strings.str_hsim_01_briefing_pla_3: Well, alright. Take it easy, ok? Catch you later.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_desc:
Hey, Tom.
Man, it feels good to get a break from Vrana contracts, y'know?

Ok. So, I've called ahead and confirmed everything with Nichols. You're all set to help them out with the Vet' show. He'll be expecting you, so just fly down there and enjoy the flight!

Don't try any manoeuvres that you're not totally comfortable with, bro, but have a great time. I know you're in safe hands with Sam.

Joe.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_1_sum:
Sling-load materials from the damaged Xiamijn Cargo ship to the Hood Storage Compound.

Regards,
M.C.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p2_03_1_desc:
CIVIL AVIATION CONTRACT
Vrana Industries Incorporated, hereafter referred to as the COMPANY, and the CONTRACTOR hereby agree to enter into a new formal arrangement hereafter referred to as the CONTRACT.

The COMPANY requires the CONTRACTOR to transport materials, under the authority of Brian Frost, Ion-Incorporated, hereafter refereed to as the CLIENT. Materials are to delivered via sling-load, from the deck of the cargo vessel Xiamijn and recovered from out of the water, to the Hood Storage Compound.

The CONTRACTOR will coordinate with CLIENT ground staff, and ensure the safe transportation of materials. Damage caused to materials or transport helicopter will result in the termination of the CONTRACT.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_sum:
Head over to Haydon's compound, follow his flight-plan, and try to find out more information about a potential business deal.

J.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_9: T:Even in the worst of times, the industry was never in this state.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_8: J:Dad would never have seen us lose our independence
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_ass_0: My goodness, what was that? Mr Larkin, do you have proper control of the helicopter?
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_ceo_0: Relax, woman. It was simply a rogue golf ball striking the fuselage. Perhaps if we were flying a little faster, Mr Larkin..?
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ass_0: So, uh, this first course is relatively close to your residence; however, it has -
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ass_1: Um, and - well - so, coming up to our second course - it is, err, rather, it can be characterised by its rather large number of bunkers -
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ass_2: Now we're approaching the third club, which is actually one of the most popular public courses, and -
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ceo_0: Stop right there. Of course I know this club. I can practically see my estate from here! I specifically instructed you to look further afield!
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ass_3: Here, I've selected something of flat course, where you'll find -
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ceo_1: Did you not read the brief? Do you think I want our clients to be hacking around in sand all day?
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ass_4: Next we're coming up to the shortest of all our courses -
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ceo_2: We're not looking to slum it, girl! We're looking for exclusivity! Do you even know what that word means?
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ass_5: Ok, well, now... our final course is private, um, happily, er, situated, and has a good reputation.
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ceo_3: Good grief, woman! You understand we are looking for something with a bit of interest?
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ceo_4: Let me stop you right there. Nine holes won't be acceptable. Mr Larkin, please skip this course.
strings.str_hsim_one_liners_golfcourses_ceo_5: Hm, I see. Well, let us take a trip around to get a clearer sense of it.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_ceo_pla_0: No, uh, I dunno... I just know he must be pretty wealthy.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_ceo_pla_1: Hold on, what? The company involved in the cargo disaster?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_ceo_sec_1: Well, I've been doing a bit of asking around about your client today - you know who he is?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_ceo_sec_2: I should say so. Turns out Haydon is CEO of a major international conglomerate - Vrana Corp. Industries.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_ceo_sec_4: Yeah, anyway, your brother has more details about the contract. Stand by.
strings.str_hsim_event_landing_ceo_0: An illuminating flight, Mr Larkin - very much indeed.
strings.str_hsim_event_landing_ceo_1: Yes, that's the spirit. Well, I shall look forward to hearing from your brother in due course.
strings.str_hsim_event_landing_pla_0: Uh, agreed, Mr Haydon. An eventful one.
strings.str_hsim_event_executive_ceo_0: Ah, Mr Larkin! It's a fine day for a tour, is it not?
strings.str_hsim_event_executive_ceo_1: No, no, Mr Larkin, you misunderstand! Today, we shall take one of my helicopters.
strings.str_hsim_event_executive_pla_0: Sure is, Mr Haydon, should we get this bird in the air?
strings.str_hsim_event_boarded_ceo_0: Take a second to get accustomed with the helicopter, Mr. Larkin.
strings.str_hsim_event_boarded_ceo_1: Please, do consult the flight plan when it suits you. My P.A. has arranged the route.
strings.str_hsim_event_boarded_ceo_2: She's selected several golf courses, which I shall be evaluating from the air.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_bro_0: Ah, Tom, good: you're here. I've had some news.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_bro_1: It seems like the buyer - Mr Haydon - is interested in conducting a little more business with us...
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_bro_2: I know, I know that... Look, he hasn't said exactly what all this is about.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_bro_3: The least we can do is meet with him - see what's on the table.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_mec_0: Well, It seems pretty clear to me.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_mec_1: We need our choppers to drum up any business at all. We can't just go on bleeding our assets, Joe.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_bro_4: Easy, Craymer. Tom is scheduled to meet with Mr Haydon - the guy that bought the chopper - he wants a meeting to discuss further business.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_mec_2: Relax, old man, Joe's just negotiating a price for our remaining assets, is all.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_revelation_sec_0: Well, now, what's this all about, boys?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_details_bro_0: Hi, Tom, it's your brother here too.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_details_bro_1: Haydon's assistant just emailed me some sorta flight plan confirmation - a short tour of some kind.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_details_bro_2: Yeah, fly safe, bro'. And, uh, sorry... sorry I didn't have this information earlier.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_details_sec_0: Find out what he's digging for, Tom, but go easy.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_details_sec_1: Concentrate on your flying and keep your cards close to your chest. You'll do just fine, son.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_04_ceo_0: The details, Tom, I can thrash out with your brother. Suffice to say, we would seek to procure a majority stake in your business.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_04_ceo_1: Of course... in return, we'd provide investment in real terms.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_04_pla_0: So, what exactly are you proposing here?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_04_ceo_2: Helicopters, equipment, skilled workers - the very lifeblood of an aviation service.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_04_ceo_3: Naturally, naturally. We'll be sending over the documents, of course - initiating the formal procedures. This simply affords us the opportunity of discussing things as men.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_04_pla_2: Sure, I see... well, of course, I'll discuss this with my brother.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_03_ceo_0: Mr Larkin, let me be frank. I would be very disappointed to see a traditional family business, such as Larkin Aviation, crumble under economic pressure.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_03_ceo_1: Consequently, I strongly believe that we could work together - a mutually beneficial relationship, as it were.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_03_ceo_2: Indeed, Tom. Well, we seek to strengthen our presence in the civil rotor-wing sector; Larkin Aviation has a strong reputation and an ideal location.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_03_ceo_3: You represent one of the business' primary assets - I sought to ascertain your capacity as a pilot, and your brother's as business manager.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_03_pla_0: Ok, well, as I understand, you're an executive in a pretty powerful conglomerate...
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_03_pla_1: Just what kinda interest would they have in Larkin Aviation?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_02_ceo_0: I think, Mr Larkin, it is about time that I put my cards on the table.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_02_ceo_1: You see, I admire Larkin Aviation; I like it very much indeed.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_02_ceo_2: Exactly - although, they do say 'pride comes before a fall', do they not, Mr Larkin?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_02_pla_0: Thank you, sir, we're all very proud of our operation.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_02_pla_1: I'm not exactly sure what you're getting at, sir...
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_01_ceo_0: So, tell me, how fares the business, Tom?
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_01_ceo_1: Certainly... certainly - one must be shrewd in such uncertain times.
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_01_ceo_2: After all, through no fault of their own, a lot of small enterprises are at real risk of folding...
strings.str_hsim_ambient_deal_01_pla_0: As well as can be expected. It's a tough time for everyone these days. Yourself?
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_6: T:Even if things were different, there'd barely be enough jobs for the both of us in this economy.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_5: T:Hey, man, this isn't on you..
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_4: J:with me grounded -- contracts at best trickling in...
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_3: J:we just don't seem to have any choice in the matter
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_2: T:Sure... I get the same feeling.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_16: J:even when we have -- VRANACORP -- emblazoned on our livery?
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_14: T:And whatever happens, this is still our business at heart...
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_12: T:I trust you to make the right decision. You've got the numbers at hand.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_10: T:Sure, he was fiercely independent, but - you know as well as I do - Dad was also a pragmatist.
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_im_1: J:yknow, I've gotta say, I'm not sure where my head is at with all this, bro
strings.str_hsim_us_core_p1_04_desc:
Tom,
So, we're still not sure exactly what the deal is here, but, this is the plan as we know it. The previous buyer of our aircraft - William Haydon - has been back in contact and has requested our services again.

You're tasked to fly out to his compound, and follow the flight plan he's had drawn up. I'm still confirming the final details with his assistant, but it seems like he's all set on taking a tour around a selection of Seattle's golf courses.

At this stage, we're not turning any work away, and I'm convinced that there's more to this job than just this. Try to find out a little more if you can, bro.

Joe.

strings.str_hsim_overview_us_campaign:
The late Harry Larkin's aviation business has fallen on tough times. Built up over decades, it's now only weeks away from closure.

His sons face an uncertain future, struggling to save the company their father spent his whole life building.

Together, they must take on contracts and competitors; together, they Take On Helicopters!
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_task_inspect1: Inspect your helicopters for damage, perform small fixes yourself and get maintenance to deal with the complicated repairs before your next flight.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_task_upgrade1: Use the heliport menu (Esc) to upgrade your fleet of helicopters. You can purchase completely new aircraft, or buy attachments and upgrades for the ones you own. It is also possible to color your helicopters however you like.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary1:
Welcome to your heliport business: Larkin Aviation.

You can access its management menu by using Esc and selecting 'Heliport'.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary10: Do you just want to fly around in your selected helicopter, select the 'Free Flight' contract and you will be ready to take to the skies!
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_task_lessons1: Use the radio to get in touch with your personal instructor, and order specific helicopter training lessons.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_task_contracts1: Take on new contracts by going to the heliport menu (Esc), seeing which contracts are available and starting the one you want. Alternatively you can speak to various people at the heliport for contracts.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_task_security1: Interact with your head of security Kelly to have him tell you about any contracts for the government.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary2:
You can (re)play any contract from the heliport 'Contracts' menu.

Select the party you wish to do a contract for, read the summary and you are good to go.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_task_manager1: Interact with your business manager Michelle to ask her about possible business contracts.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary3: In the 'Personal' section you will find a Instant Messaging history related to previously played contracts, between you and various other characters.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_task_brother1: Interact with your brother Joe to have him tell you about the next available contract opportunity.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary4: From the 'Helicopters' menu you are able to assign your personal helicopter, purchase new helicopters, buy upgrades and do repairs.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary5:
In the 'Helicopters' menu select a helicopter from the list and select 'Assign Pilot'.

Unless a contract requires a specific helicopter, this will now be the helicopter you fly.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary6: You may buy more helicopters if you have enough money, or sell helicopters you already own (you must always keep one).
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary7:
Helicopters can be upgraded by various parts, such as exterior components, cabin improvements and paint schemes.

Some functional upgrades exist as well. Buying a winch system for example will open up various Search and Rescue contracts.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary8:
Damage to your helicopters is persistent, so make sure to perform regular inspections.

Walk to the helicopter and look at various components and / or interact with them to find unknown damages.

The more damages you identify, the cheaper the repair will be.
strings.str_hsim_united_states_h_diary9:
You can repair damages to your helicopters from the 'Helicopters' menu.

Select the '<Helicopter>' category and '<Maintenance>' subcategory and perform the repairs.

strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_9: At high speeds it is necessary to bank (lean) the whole helicopter, when you want to change your heading. This is done by pulling the cyclic controller left and right.
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_7: Use %2 to press on the right pedal - to yaw right!
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_5: You can effectively yaw (rotate) the chopper left and right only while hovering or flying at low speeds.
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_4: Use %1 to press on the left pedal - to yaw left!
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_3: The pedals on the floor are used to control the yaw - to rotate the helicopter around the vertical axis.
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_18: Use %2 pull the cyclic aftwards - to decrease the speed!
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_17: To decrease the chopper's speed, you need to pull the cyclic aftwards (backwards).
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_15: Use %1 to push the cyclic forward - to increase the speed!
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_14: Pushing the cyclic forward will increase the rotor blades angle of attack. This will increase the forward pull and speed. As a side effect it will also cause the helicopter to pitch down slightly.
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_12: Use %2 to pull the cyclic right - to bank the helicopter right.
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_10: Use %1 to pull the cyclic left - to bank the helicopter left.
strings.str_hsim_3_controls.sqf_1: Turn off the auto-hover from the action menu or by pressing the %1.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_8: Use %1 to increase collective & take off!
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_7: With enough vertical lift, the chopper will take off and will start to climb.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_5: The 'collective pitch control', a lever found at your left-hand side, is used to adjust the angle of the rotor blades. Collective directly influences vertical lift of the helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_3: The 'auto hover' system can be activated by selecting the 'Auto-hover On' action from the action menu or by pressing %1.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_16: Unless you lower the collective, the helicopter will continue to climb.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_14: Press %2 to lower the collective and start to descend.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_13: Unless you lower the collective, the helicopter will continue to climb.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_10: Press %1 to increase the collective and gain some altitude.
strings.str_hsim_2_altitude.sqf_1: Before we lift off for the first time, turn on the auto hover system. It will greatly help you to keep the helicopter stable in the air.

strings.str_hsim_cfgbase_united_states_h_helicop:
Dad's first utility helicopter, the one which helped put Larkin Aviation on the map. He bought it second hand in the early 90s, and it's served us well more almost two decades now.

Sadly, it's maintenance cost has become a burden in these tough times. Craymer managed to get in contact with some buyer who's apparently interested in these vintage machines.

It deserves a good home.

strings.str_hsim_endquote_1:
'Helicopters don't fly. They just beat the air into submission'.
- Unknown
strings.str_hsim_endquote_2: 'Helicopters are the only aircraft in the US Military that take bird strikes in the rear.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_3: 'If it's ugly, it's British; if it's weird, it's French; and if it's ugly and weird, it's Russian.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_4: 'The only time you have too much fuel is when you're on fire.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_5: 'Hovering is for people who love to fly but have no place to go.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_6: 'Helicopters are a collection of parts flying in relatively close formation while all rotating around different axis. This arrangement works work well until one of the parts breaks formation.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_7: 'Always try to keep the number of times you park the helicopter equal to the number of times you've flown it.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_8: 'How do you make 1 million dollars flying helicopters? Start with 2 million.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_9: 'In the ongoing battle between objects made of aluminum and glass going dozens of miles per hour, and the ground going zero miles per hour, the ground has yet to lose. Draws don't count.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_10:
'That's not flying, that's just falling with style!'
- Woody (Toy Story 1995)
strings.str_hsim_endquote_11:
'Newton's Law states that what goes up, must come down. Our Company Commander's Law states that what goes up and comes down had damn well better be able to go back up again.'
- 187th Assault Helicopter Company, Tay Ninh, Viet Nam, 1971.
strings.str_hsim_endquote_12:
'I never liked riding in helicopters because there's a fair probability that the bottom part will get going around as fast as the top part.'
- Lt. Col. John Wittenborn, USAF.
strings.str_hsim_endquote_13:
'You can always tell a helicopter pilot in anything moving - a train, an airplane, a car or a boat. They never smile, they are always listening to the machine and they always hear something they think is not right.'
- Col. Charlie Block, USMC
strings.str_hsim_endquote_14:
'Even a perfectly executed autorotation only gives you a glide ratio slightly better than that of a brick.'
- Col. Charlie Block, USMC.
strings.str_hsim_endquote_15:
'If everything is working fine on your helicopter consider yourself temporarily lucky. Something is about to break.'
- Col. Charlie Block, USMC.
strings.str_hsim_endquote_16:
'In general, airplane pilots are open, clear-eyed, buoyant extroverts and helicopter pilots are brooding introspective anticipators of trouble. They know if something bad has not happened it is about to.'
- Harry Reasoner (1971)
strings.str_hsim_endquote_17:
'I went on to fly over 11,000 hours in jets, props and helicopters before hanging up my wings. What I miss most is skimming over the trees at 100 knots, all by myself in a light observation helicopter.'
- Harry Reasoner (1971)
strings.str_hsim_endquote_18: 'If the wings are travelling faster than the fuselage, it's probably a helicopter - and therefore, unsafe.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_19: 'Chuck Norris invented the helicopter by performing 20 round house kicks in a row.'
strings.str_hsim_endquote_20: 'When one engine fails on a twin-engine helicopter, you always have enough power left to get you to the scene of the crash.'
strings.str_hsim_brother_h0_info:
Harry Larkin's eldest son, Joe is passionate about his family's business - desperate for it to succeed despite the difficult circumstances.

An experienced pilot - serving two tours of duty in the armed forces - Joe's an enthusiastic guy, a person who tries to find the best in any given situation. Joe is a man under a lot of pressure
strings.str_hsim_ceo_h0_info:
William Haydon is successful and powerful businessman with a keen admiration of Larkin Aviation, and their well-positioned heliport, Highland Park.

Well-spoken and highly educated, Mr. Haydon is a confident and successful executive with connections and an eye for business opportunities.
strings.str_hsim_frost_h0_info:
Frost is a an ex-British Armed Forces paratrooper and security contractor with a wealth of combat experience. Well-trained, self-confident and authoritative, Frost's experiences have made him the man he is today.

Currently working a Head of Operations for ION, Inc - a subsidiary of Vrana Corp - Frost is used in various roles, from training exercises to corporate security activities.
strings.str_hsim_instructor_h0_info:
Recently retired after a long career of distinguished service in the U.S. Marine Corp, Maddox is a veteran pilot of numerous campaigns, and is the man you want flying your helicopter.

Maddox settled down in his native Seattle, opening a flight school to teach the next generation of fly-boys a thing or too.
strings.str_hsim_maintenance_h0_info:
Low on funds - and with ageing parents to support - Craymer dropped out of his aeronautical engineering degree in his Sophomore year to work for Larkin Aviation.

Often able to identify a problem just by listening to the sounds of the helicopter, Craymer is a passionate and enthusiastic individual that loves all things helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_manager_h0_info:
Michelle Carmichael is a young business professional with a sharp mind and bright future. Specialising in business management consultancy, she's well equipped to turn around struggling companies in the toughest of economic circumstances.

Moving to Washington from the UK to complete her masters, she quickly found stability, entering into a fast-track graduate programme with Vrana Corp. Industries.
strings.str_hsim_player_h0_info:
Taking a different path in life than his brother, Tom Larkin moved away to college at the first opportunity. Although inexperienced with helicopters, Tom always remained proud of and dedicated to his family.

The unexpected death of his father came as a real blow. Taking a break from his studies to spend time supporting his family, Tom has the chance to learn a lot more about his father and a business that he knows next to nothing about.
strings.str_hsim_security_h0_info:
Paul Kelly works for the Larkins, providing location management and security on site at Highland Park Heliport.

Kelly retired from the SPD years earlier, but - an old friend of the family - he came back to work for Larkin Aviation shortly before Harry Larkin passed away.
strings.str_hsim_lib_ied: Импровизированные взрывные устройства (Improvised Explosive Devices - IEDs), или просто фугасы, - это, как правило, самодельные бомбы, скрытно устанавливаемые боевиками на дорогах для атак на военные конвои. Во время Иракской войны, начавшейся в 2003 году, большинство потерь коалиционных войск было связано именно с фугасами. Самодельные фугасы делают из самых разнообразных материалов, используя при этом различные виды детонаторов. Это делает их невероятно сложными для обнаружения и разминирования.

strings.str_hsim_credits_role26: Our unnamed private pilot and mechanic
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_medium01_sheri:
A medium helicopter variant - custom-tailored for the State Sheriff's Office - identified by its unique paint scheme and markings. It comes equipped with a powerful searchlight to illuminate the environment in low-visibility conditions.

This helicopter is also frequently used to deploy tactical law enforcement officers by means of fast-rope insertion. The ropes are attached to both sides of the cabin, enabling officers to quickly rope down. Once everyone is safely on the ground, the ropes are detached.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_medium01_veter:
Used primarily in air shows and memorial events, this is a heavily modified military helicopter. Its distinct shape reminds all of those who took part in them of various military conflicts around the world.

The striking shark's mouth paint scheme was used to express a form of individuality, but also caused fear in the enemy forces encountering the aircraft.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_medium01_milit:
While often used in civilian roles, the medium helicopter is perhaps even more well-known for its military service. This armed variant features unguided rocket pods on both sides, as well as heavy multi-barrel machine guns for door gunners.

It can be expanded by various advanced systems and components, such as Forward-Looking InfraRed, a searchlight, a winch and cargo hooks.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_medium01_medic:
This is the specially-equipped Search and Rescue variant of the medium class of helicopters. Its interior caters for in-flight medical assistance, and it features wider side-doors that offer more cabin space to patients on stretchers.

Finding casualties stranded in hard-to-reach locations is assisted by a searchlight. Getting them aboard can be achieved through the use of a winch system, which lowers a rescue-worker down, attaches the casualty to his harness and raises them both towards the helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_medium01_luxur:
The executive and VIP market is expanding rapidly, and these types of client require more luxurious and comfortable helicopter configurations.

The executive model of the medium helicopter has an interior cabin with large leather seats and high quality interior finishing and details.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_medium01_flir_:
Law enforcement agencies all over the world will often call in air support when locating, observing and tracking suspects.

This variant supports a Tactical Flight Officer (TFO) to monitor and analyse the helicopter’s real-time video feeds from inside the cockpit. A searchlight and Forward-Looking InfraRed system help the TFO to work during the night and in low-visibility conditions.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_heavy_base_arm:
A large and powerful workhorse that can be used for heavy external (sling-load) and internal (cargo) transport operations.

This modern twin-engine helicopter has enough interior space to transport large payloads or fully loaded squads of military personnel. Furthermore, it has enough horsepower to be able to lift heavy external loads, including small vehicles.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_heavy_luxury_a:
The executive and VIP market is expanding rapidly, and these types of client require more luxurious and comfortable helicopter configurations.

The executive model of the heavy helicopter has an interior cabin with large leather seats and high quality interior finishing and details.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_heavy_military:
While primarily a utility helicopter - used to ferry troops from point A to B - this variant has a machine gun mounted on the rear cargo ramp for defensive purposes.

Its large interior payload and sling load capabilities make it an effective aircraft for quickly deploying goods and personnel to Forward Operating Bases across a variety of theatres.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_light01_base_a:
The lightest class of helicopter available, it is best characterised by its agile and responsive behaviour. The helicopter typically seats four to five people; a pilot and copilot in the front and either two or three passengers in the back.

Throughout its lifespan this range of helicopter has undergone various revisions. Some featured an additional main rotor blade, bringing the total to five. Other differences included increased engine power and anti-torque systems.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_light01_ion_ar:
Like many operators flying the light helicopter in tactical environments, the ION Private Military Company has painted their aircraft fully black and fitted exterior benches, enabling passengers to face out the side of the chopper.

Law enforcement, military and security personnel can quickly mount and dismount from these benches in combat zones. They also have more freedom of movement while in flight with all of their equipment. This configuration allows for two pilots and four passengers to be transported.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_light01_milita:
Aside from being used as an unarmed observation helicopter, the light helicopter also comes equipped with various weapons systems. This model has two multi-barrel and high rate of fire machine guns mounted on small wings. Aside from these, pilots have access to two unguided rocket pods.

To aid target tracking and night operations, the helicopter has an exterior Forward-Looking InfraRed (FLIR) dome mounted. The flight crew can find and track thermal signatures from within the cockpit.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_light01_old_ar:
An older model of the lightest class of helicopter, it is equipped with a less powerful engine and is therefore more suitable for training purposes involving less-experienced pilots.

This variant is also not as well suited for hot and high work, meaning it is not adapted for flying at high altitudes or in hot ambient temperatures. Both result in lower air density, which in turn provides the helicopter with less lift.
strings.str_hsim_cfgvehicles_heli_medium01_base_:
With its four-blade composite main rotor system, this is a proven multi-role helicopter capable of many emergency rescue and law enforcement roles. It replaces an older, but similar model which featured only two rotor blades.

The helicopter is known for its reliability in extreme conditions and climates. It has a large cabin which can cater for cargo or up to thirteen passengers. The tough construction and bulkheads provide protection to those inside in case of roll-over. Having two engines also allows the aircraft to land even after a full single engine malfunction.

strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_throttlecomplex: Once the 'throttle' is set to 'full', the governor takes over and controls the fuel induction to the engine.
The engine then drives the main transmission and the tail rotor transmission, which transfers power to the main rotor system and tail rotor.
The 'throttle' controls the introduction of fuel to the engine.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_throttlebasic_3: The 'throttle' has a governor and is set to 'full' to achieve the revolutions per minutes required for flight (RPM).
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_throttlebasic_1: The 'throttle' controls how much fuel is delivered to the engine.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_pedalscomplex_3: Anti-torque 'pedals' are used to control trim in flight and rotational or yaw movement in hover.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_pedalscomplex_2: 'Pedal' pressure should be adjusted when the main rotor torque changes or your heading changes.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_pedalscomplex_1: Torque-induced yaw is caused by the main rotor.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_pedalsbasic_3: Use the ''pedals'' to neutralize rotational movement caused by the main rotor.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_pedalsbasic_2: Pedal pressure can be used to rotate the helicopter.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_pedalsbasic_1: The pedals control the power delivered to the tail rotor.

strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc4_2: In this case first calibrate them in their drivers or controls panel.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc4_1: Your controller inputs may read values other than zero while in a neutral position.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc3_2: They show you the position and distance (transparency) of nearby objects, vehicles and persons.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc3_1: The colored dots that appear around your screen's edges are periphery indicators.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc2_2: Do not apply theory from the game to real helicopters and always contact a licensed instructor instead.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc2_1: Take On Helicopters is a game and it was not developed to train real-life helicopter systems, procedures or skills.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc12_3: When starting in-flight, set it to around 70%.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc12_2: When starting on the ground, ensure your collective is fully down.

strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport9_2: Select the '<Helicopter>' category and '<Maintenance>' subcategory and perform the repairs.

strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport8_3: The more damages you identify, the cheaper the repair will be.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport8_2: Walk to the helicopter and look at various components and / or interact with them to find unknown damages.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport8_1: Damage to your helicopters is persistent, so make sure to perform regular inspections.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport7_2: Some functional upgrades exist as well. Buying a winch system for example will open up various Search and Rescue contracts.

strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport4_1: From the 'Helicopters' menu you are able to assign your personal helicopter, purchase new helicopters, buy upgrades and do repairs.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport3_1: In the 'Personal' section you will find a Instant Messaging history related to previously played contracts, between you and various other characters.

strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_heliport10_1: If you just want to fly around in your selected helicopter, select the 'Free Flight' contract and you will be ready to take to the skies!
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_cycliccomplex_3: Pitching the nose by use of the 'cyclic' increases or decreases air speed.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_cycliccomplex_2: Adjustments to the 'cyclic' affects the angle of the rotor-disc.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_cyclicbasic_4: Tilt the 'cyclic' to the left or right to bank the copter.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_cyclicbasic_3: Tilt the 'cyclic' forwards or aft to raise and lower the nose.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_cyclicbasic_2: The 'cyclic' controls the tilt-angle of the main-rotor.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_collectivecompl: If you want to climb or descend, either increase or decrease the 'collective' as desired.
Raising the 'collective' increases the angle that the air-foil - that is, the blade - passes through the air, producing lift.
Lift - rotor RPM - is created when the 'collective' pitch control is raised.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_collectivebasic: Increasing the 'collective' generates more lift; lowering the collective reduces it.
'Lift' is an upward force created by airflow around the rotor-blades.
Use the 'collective' pitch control to affect lift.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_attitudecomplex: Pitching the 'attitude' down will increase airspeed and reduce height if not corrected by increasing the 'collective'.
Pitching the 'attitude' up will reduce airspeed and increase the height if not corrected by reducing the 'collective'.
Use the 'cyclic' to pitch the aircraft and change the 'attitude', which in turn changes the airspeed.
'Attitude' describes the pitch angle of a helicopter as it moves through the air.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_attitudebasic_3: Pitching the nose up will increase height, and will reduce speed.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_attitudebasic_2: Pitching the nose down will increase speed, and will reduce height.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_attitudebasic_1: 'Attitude' describes the pitch of a helicopter as it moves through the air.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_benchmarks_2: Just get a new PC? Want to see how it compares to others? Run the benchmarks to find out!
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_hotstart_1: Engine temperatures should be below 200 °C before throttles are opened.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_hotstart_2: Prior to engaging full throttle, the temperature should not exceed 450 °C.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_hotstart_3: Carefully monitor and immediately close throttles in case of dangerous temperatures.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_misc9_2: Check the community hub at http://community.bistudio.com for detailed information.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_overspeed_1: When the helicopter's horizontal speed is too high, the rotating blades of main rotor can become unstable and stall.
strings.str_hsim_cfgloadingtexts_overspeed_2: The phenomena is called "retreating blade stall". To recover from its effect, first reduce the collective, then pitch the nose up to reduce airspeed.
strings.str_hsim_difficulty_0:
This mode is designed for players that are completely new to either our game, to flying helicopters, or both!

Flight Dynamics: Many simulation helpers are at your disposal; several are active by default to help get you going - great for keeping you in the air!

Gameplay: Waypoints and tasks are visible in the 3D world, and you can activate various other visual aids - great for getting the job done!

Note: You can still configure various difficulty/ flight dynamics settings from their default values, so you can get started with as much or as little support as you prefer!
strings.str_hsim_difficulty_1:
This mode is designed for players that are either new to our game or to the higher-fidelity flight dynamics, but who are familiar with the general principles.

Flight Dynamics: Some flight dynamics helpers are disabled, although others are still at your disposal - great for getting a challenge from the flight model!

Gameplay: Some gameplay helpers are disabled by default, and working out what to do will be less obvious - great for getting a challenge from the game!


Note: You can still configure various difficulty/ flight-dynamics settings from their default values, although some will be locked!

If you're a veteran helicopter pilot, you might select this mode until you're comfortable with many gameplay features and conventions.

You can disable individual flight-dynamics helpers to give you the full experience, while retaining some of the gameplay guides.
strings.str_hsim_difficulty_2:
This mode is designed for players that are experienced both with our game and complex flight models!

Flight Dynamics: Many simulation helpers are disabled and locked; you'll have to work to keep the bird in the air - great for getting the full experience of our new flight models!

Gameplay: Many guides are disabled by default; you'll have to study your tasks carefully and keep an eye on your instrument panel - Great for getting totally engaged with the tasks at hand!

Note: you can still configure various difficulty/ flight dynamics settings from their default values, although many will be locked. You should play in this mode once you're comfortable with completing tasks and keeping the helicopter in the air.

strings.str_cup_lib_av8b: The McDonnell Douglas (now Boeing) AV-8B Harrier II is a single-engine ground-attack aircraft that constitutes the second generation of the Harrier Jump Jet family. Capable of vertical or short takeoff and landing (V/STOL), the aircraft was designed in the late 1970s as an Anglo-American development of the British Hawker Siddeley Harrier, the first operational V/STOL aircraft. Named after a bird of prey,[6] it is primarily employed on light attack or multi-role missions, ranging from close air support of ground troops to armed reconnaissance.
strings.str_cup_lib_gr9: The British Aerospace Harrier II is a second-generation vertical/short takeoff and landing (V/STOL) jet aircraft used previously by the Royal Air Force (RAF) and, between 2006 and 2010, the Royal Navy (RN). The aircraft was derived from the McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II, which itself was a development of the Hawker Siddeley Harrier. Initial deliveries of the Harrier II were designated in service as Harrier GR5; subsequently upgraded airframes were redesignated accordingly as GR7 and GR9.
strings.str_cup_lib_ch47:
CH-47 'Чинук' - многоцелевой тяжелый военно-транспортный вертолет двухвинтовой продольной схемы. Он развивал скорость в 315 км/ч и был куда быстрее аналогичных машин в 60-е, да и по сей день такие скорости доступны не всем.
CH-47 используется, в основном, для переброски войск, организации снабжения в боевых условиях и перевозки артиллерийских орудий.

strings.str_cup_lib_m60a3: The M60 served as the primary U.S. main battle tank of the Cold War. The M60A3 variant features a number of technological enhancements, including smoke dischargers, a new rangefinder, a ballistic computer and a turret stabilization system. All active American M60s eventually underwent the conversion to the A3 model. Phased out of U.S. service in the early 1990s, the M60-series tanks continue to serve as front-line MBTs in more than twenty countries.

strings.str_cup_lib_aa12:
АА-12 - это дробовик с возможностью ведения автоматического огня со скоростью примерно 300 выстрелов в минуту, что делает его невероятно смертоносным оружием в условиях ограниченных пространств, таких как городские кварталы. В нем могут быть использованы различные боеприпасы, например, дробь или разрывные патроны.

Диксон, охранник в компании ION Inc. выдумал для своего любимого дробовика прозвище 'Матильда'.
strings.str_cup_lib_acr:
The Remington Adaptive Combat Rifle (ACR) is an assault rifle with a modular design, conceptualized by Magpul Industries, produced by Bushmaster to civilian sale and by Remington for military sale.

The ACR comes in a number of variants, chambered in 5.56 NATO and 6.8 SPC, with carbine, rifle and marksman barrel lengths, and option for a EGLM underbarrel grenade launcher.
strings.str_cup_lib_akm:
Автомат АКМ - это улучшенный вариант всемирно известного АК-47, разработанный в пятидесятые годы. АКМ - это самый распространенный автомат Калашникова.
По сравнению с АК-47 автомат АКМ оптимизирован под массовое производство. В результате его масса сократилась на 1 кг, значительно увеличилась точность и повысилась надежность.
strings.str_cup_lib_ak74: АК-74 - наследник знаменитого АК-47, с калибром, уменьшенным до 5,45 мм, что стало ответом на введение патрона калибра 5,56 мм в НАТО. Наиболее очевидным нововведением стал дульный тормоз. Он значительно ослабляет и без того скромную отдачу АК-74, но увеличивает вспышку и громкость звука при выстреле.
strings.str_cup_lib_ak47: Знаменитый АК-47. Разработанный и сконструированный в 1950ых, он быстро стал самым известным из всего огнестрельного оружия в мире.
strings.str_cup_lib_ak107:
АК-107 - российский автомат калибра 5,45 мм, разработанный на основе серии АК-100. Автомат отчается сбалансированной автоматикой. Благодаря этому заметно снижается сила отдачи, что позволяет значительно увеличить точность стрельбы при ведении автоматического огня.
Данная модель оснащена оптическим прицелом ПСО-1.
strings.str_cup_lib_aks74:
АКС-74 - это вариант автомата АК-74 со складным вбок металлическим прикладом, созданный для вооружения Воздушно-десантных войск СССР. Калибр патронов автомата - 5.45х39 мм, переход на который с калибра 7.62х39 мм обусловлен желанием создать эквивалент распространенному боеприпасу НАТО - промежуточному патрону 5.56х45 мм.
Данный образец оснащен электронным коллиматорным прицелом 'Кобра', настроенным для ведения боя в ночных условиях.
strings.str_cup_lib_aks74u:
АКС-74У - это личное стрелковое оружие для вооружения экипажей бронетехники и вертолетов, а также для отрядов особого назначения, которым нужно компактное и относительно убойное оружие 'в одном флаконе'.
Преимущество небольшого по размерам АКС-74У состоит в том, что он использует стандартные автоматные патроны.
strings.str_cup_lib_aks: Автомат АКС - это модификация автомата АК-47. Он обладает складным прикладом и предназначен для экипажей техники и воздушно-десантных войск.
strings.str_cup_lib_rpk:
РПК-74 - ручной пулемет, появившийся в 1974 году. Это модифицированный вариант автомата АК-74. При модификации были проведены те же изменения, что и в случае АКМ.
Для РПК-74 используются патроны 5.45x39 мм.
